Original range: 683-733
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether the reference collection describes a variable that
     * is initialized to an immutable value, never modified, and defined before
     * every reference.
     */
Method code:
683 |     private boolean isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var v,
684 |         ReferenceCollection refInfo) {
685 |       List<Reference> refSet = refInfo.references;
686 |       int startingReadRef = 1;
687 |       Reference refDecl = refSet.get(0);
688 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(refDecl)) {
689 |         return false;
690 |       }
691 | 
692 |       boolean isNeverAssigned = refInfo.isNeverAssigned();
693 |       // For values that are never assigned, only the references need to be
694 |       // checked.
695 |       if (!isNeverAssigned) {
696 |         Reference refInit = refInfo.getInitializingReference();
697 |         if (!isValidInitialization(refInit)) {
698 |           return false;
699 |         }
700 | 
701 |         if (refDecl != refInit) {
702 |           Preconditions.checkState(refInit == refSet.get(1));
703 |           startingReadRef = 2;
704 |         }
705 | 
706 |         if (!refInfo.isWellDefined()) {
707 |           return false;
708 |         }
709 | 
710 |         Node value = refInit.getAssignedValue();
711 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
712 | 
713 |         boolean isImmutableValueWorthInlining =
714 |             NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value) &&
715 |             (!value.isString() ||
716 |                 isStringWorthInlining(v, refInfo.references));
717 |         boolean isInlinableThisAlias =
718 |             value.isThis() &&
719 |             !refInfo.isEscaped();
720 |         if (!isImmutableValueWorthInlining && !isInlinableThisAlias) {
721 |           return false;
722 |         }
723 |       }
724 | 
725 |       for (int i = startingReadRef; i < refSet.size(); i++) {
726 |         Reference ref = refSet.get(i);
727 |         if (!isValidReference(ref)) {
728 |           return false;
729 |         }
730 |       }
731 | 
732 |       return true;
733 |     }

477 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")

===== M0028 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 704-753
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assignments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
704 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
705 |     boolean changes = false;
706 |     do {
707 |       changes = false;
708 | 
709 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
710 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
711 |       // we traverse it.
712 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
713 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
714 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
715 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
716 |           current--;
717 |         } else {
718 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
719 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
720 | 
721 |           if (var.getParentNode().isVar() &&
722 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
723 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
724 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
725 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
726 |           } else {
727 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
728 |             // or a for...in variable.
729 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
730 |           }
731 | 
732 |           boolean maybeEscaped = false;
733 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
734 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
735 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
736 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
737 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
738 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
739 |             }
740 |             if (assign.maybeAliased) {
741 |               maybeEscaped = true;
742 |             }
743 |           }
744 | 
745 |           if ((assignedToUnknownValue || maybeEscaped) && hasPropertyAssign) {
746 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
747 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
748 |             current--;
749 |           }
750 |         }
751 |       }
752 |     } while (changes);
753 |   }

57 |            current = current.getParent()) {
58 |         int type = current.getType();
59 |         JSDocInfo info = null;
60 | 
61 |         // We only care about function annotations at the FUNCTION and SCRIPT
62 |         // level. Otherwise, the @suppress annotation has an implicit
63 |         // dependency on the exact structure of our AST, and that seems like
64 |         // a bad idea.
65 |         if (type == Token.FUNCTION) {
66 |           info = NodeUtil.getFunctionJSDocInfo(current);
67 |         } else if (type == Token.SCRIPT) {
68 |           info = current.getJSDocInfo();
69 |         } else if (type == Token.ASSIGN) {
70 |           Node rhs = current.getLastChild();
71 |           if (rhs.isFunction()) {
72 |             info = NodeUtil.getFunctionJSDocInfo(rhs);
73 |           }
74 |         }
75 | 
76 |         if (info != null) {
77 |           for (String suppressor : info.getSuppressions()) {
78 |             WarningsGuard guard = suppressors.get(suppressor);
79 | 
80 |             // Some @suppress tags are for other tools, and
81 |             // may not have a warnings guard.
82 |             if (guard != null) {
83 |               CheckLevel newLevel = guard.level(error);
84 |               if (newLevel != null) {
85 |                 return newLevel;
86 |               }
87 |             }
88 |           }
89 |         }
90 |       }
91 |     }
92 |     return null;
93 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal.traverseFunction(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeTraversal.java
Original range: 511-546
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses a function.
   */
Method code:
511 |   private void traverseFunction(Node n, Node parent) {
512 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
513 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isFunction());
514 | 
515 |     final Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
516 | 
517 |     boolean isFunctionExpression = (parent != null)
518 |         && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n);
519 | 
520 |     if (!isFunctionExpression) {
521 |       // Functions declarations are in the scope containing the declaration.
522 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
523 |     }
524 | 
525 |     curNode = n;
526 |     pushScope(n);
527 | 
528 |     if (isFunctionExpression) {
529 |       // Function expression names are only accessible within the function
530 |       // scope.
531 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
532 |     }
533 | 
534 |     final Node args = fnName.getNext();
535 |     final Node body = args.getNext();
536 | 
537 |     // Args
538 |     traverseBranch(args, n);
539 | 
540 |     // Body
541 |     Preconditions.checkState(body.getNext() == null &&
542 |             body.isBlock(), body);
543 |     traverseBranch(body, n);
544 | 
545 |     popScope();
546 |   }

Documentation:
/** Creates the passes for the main optimization loop. */
Method code:
678 |   private List<PassFactory> getMainOptimizationLoop() {
679 |     List<PassFactory> passes = Lists.newArrayList();
680 |     if (options.inlineGetters) {
681 |       passes.add(inlineSimpleMethods);
682 |     }
683 | 
684 |     passes.addAll(getCodeRemovingPasses());
685 | 
686 |     if (options.inlineFunctions || options.inlineLocalFunctions) {
687 |       passes.add(inlineFunctions);
688 |     }
689 | 
690 |     if (options.inlineProperties) {
691 |       passes.add(inlineProperties);
692 |     }
693 | 
694 |     boolean runOptimizeCalls = options.optimizeCalls
695 |         || options.optimizeParameters
696 |         || options.optimizeReturns;
697 | 
698 |     if (options.removeUnusedVars || options.removeUnusedLocalVars) {
699 |       if (options.deadAssignmentElimination) {
700 |         passes.add(deadAssignmentsElimination);
701 |       }
702 |       if (!runOptimizeCalls) {
703 |         passes.add(removeUnusedVars);
704 |       }
705 |     }
706 |     if (runOptimizeCalls) {
707 |       passes.add(optimizeCallsAndRemoveUnusedVars);
708 |     }
709 |     assertAllLoopablePasses(passes);
710 |     return passes;
711 |   }

121 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {

123 |         compiler, new NormalizeStatements(compiler, assertOnChange))
124 |         .traverseRoots(externs, root);
125 |     if (MAKE_LOCAL_NAMES_UNIQUE) {
126 |       MakeDeclaredNamesUnique renamer = new MakeDeclaredNamesUnique();
127 |       NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, renamer);
128 |       t.traverseRoots(externs, root);
129 |     }
130 |     // It is important that removeDuplicateDeclarations runs after
131 |     // MakeDeclaredNamesUnique in order for catch block exception names to be
132 |     // handled properly. Specifically, catch block exception names are
133 |     // only valid within the catch block, but our current Scope logic
134 |     // has no concept of this and includes it in the containing function
135 |     // (or global scope). MakeDeclaredNamesUnique makes the catch exception
136 |     // names unique so that removeDuplicateDeclarations() will properly handle
137 |     // cases where a function scope variable conflict with a exception name:
138 |     //   function f() {
139 |     //      try {throw 0;} catch(e) {e; /* catch scope 'e'*/}
140 |     //      var e = 1; // f scope 'e'
141 |     //   }
142 |     // otherwise 'var e = 1' would be rewritten as 'e = 1'.
143 |     // TODO(johnlenz): Introduce a separate scope for catch nodes.
144 |     removeDuplicateDeclarations(externs, root);
145 |     new PropagateConstantAnnotationsOverVars(compiler, assertOnChange)
146 |         .process(externs, root);
147 | 
148 |     FindExposeAnnotations findExposeAnnotations = new FindExposeAnnotations();
149 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, findExposeAnnotations);
150 |     if (!findExposeAnnotations.exposedProperties.isEmpty()) {
151 |       NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root,
152 |           new RewriteExposedProperties(
153 |               findExposeAnnotations.exposedProperties));
154 |     }
155 |

157 |       compiler.setLifeCycleStage(LifeCycleStage.NORMALIZED);
158 |     }

Method code:
288 |   public void traverseRoots(List<Node> roots) {
289 |     if (roots.isEmpty()) {
290 |       return;
291 |     }
292 | 
293 |     try {
294 |       Node scopeRoot = roots.get(0).getParent();
295 |       Preconditions.checkState(scopeRoot != null);
296 | 
297 |       inputId = NodeUtil.getInputId(scopeRoot);
298 |       sourceName = "";
299 |       curNode = scopeRoot;
300 |       pushScope(scopeRoot);
301 |

303 |         Preconditions.checkState(root.getParent() == scopeRoot);
304 |         traverseBranch(root, scopeRoot);
305 |       }

308 |     } catch (Exception unexpectedException) {
309 |       throwUnexpectedException(unexpectedException);
310 |     }

===== M0076 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.compileInternal()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 704-749
Documentation:

Method code:
704 |   private void compileInternal() {
705 |     setProgress(0.0);
706 |     parse();
707 |     // 15 percent of the work is assumed to be for parsing (based on some
708 |     // minimal analysis on big JS projects, of course this depends on options)
709 |     setProgress(0.15);
710 |     if (hasErrors()) {
711 |       return;
712 |     }
713 | 
714 |     if (!precheck()) {
715 |       return;
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     if (options.nameAnonymousFunctionsOnly) {
719 |       // TODO(nicksantos): Move this into an instrument() phase maybe?
720 |       check();
721 |       return;
722 |     }
723 | 
724 |     if (!options.skipAllPasses) {
725 |       check();
726 |       if (hasErrors()) {
727 |         return;
728 |       }
729 | 
730 |       if (options.isExternExportsEnabled()
731 |           || options.externExportsPath != null) {
732 |         externExports();
733 |       }
734 | 
735 |       // IDE-mode is defined to stop here, before the heavy rewriting begins.
736 |       if (!options.ideMode) {
737 |         optimize();
738 |       }
739 |     }
740 | 
741 |     if (options.recordFunctionInformation) {
742 |       recordFunctionInformation();
743 |     }
744 | 
745 |     if (options.devMode == DevMode.START_AND_END) {
746 |       runSanityCheck();
747 |     }
748 |     setProgress(1.0);
749 |   }

===== M0108 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeConsumer.addNumber(double)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeConsumer.java
Original range: 240-276
Documentation:

Method code:
240 |   void addNumber(double x) {
241 |     // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of x- -4 as
242 |     // x--4 (which is a syntax error).
243 |     char prev = getLastChar();
244 |     boolean negativeZero = isNegativeZero(x);
245 |     if ((x < 0 || negativeZero) && prev == '-') {
246 |       add(" ");
247 |     }
248 | 
249 |     if (negativeZero) {
250 |       addConstant("-0");
251 |     } else if ((long) x == x) {
252 |       long value = (long) x;
253 |       long mantissa = value;
254 |       int exp = 0;
255 |       if (Math.abs(x) >= 100) {
256 |         while (mantissa / 10 * Math.pow(10, exp + 1) == value) {
257 |           mantissa /= 10;
258 |           exp++;
259 |         }
260 |       }
261 |       if (exp > 2) {
262 |         addConstant(Long.toString(mantissa) + "E" + Integer.toString(exp));
263 |       } else {
264 |         long valueAbs = Math.abs(value);
265 |         if (Long.toHexString(valueAbs).length() + 2 <
266 |             Long.toString(valueAbs).length()) {
267 |           addConstant((value < 0 ? "-" : "") + "0x" +
268 |               Long.toHexString(valueAbs));
269 |         } else {
270 |           addConstant(Long.toString(value));
271 |         }
272 |       }
273 |     } else {
274 |       addConstant(String.valueOf(x).replace(".0E", "E"));
275 |     }
276 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

120 |   @Override
121 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
122 |     if (!n.isName()) {
123 |       return;
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     String varName = n.getString();
127 | 
128 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
129 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
130 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent));
132 |       return;
133 |     }
134 | 
135 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
136 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
137 |     if ((parent.isVar() ||
138 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
139 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
140 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
141 | 
142 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
146 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
147 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
148 |     if (var == null) {
149 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
150 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
151 |         // current scope.
152 |       } else {
153 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
154 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
155 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
156 |         }
157 | 
158 |         if (sanityCheck) {
159 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
160 |         } else {
161 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
162 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
163 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
164 |         }
165 |       }
166 |       return;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
170 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
171 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
172 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
173 |       return;
174 |     }
175 | 
176 |     // Check module dependencies.
177 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
178 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
179 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
180 |     if (!sanityCheck &&
181 |         varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
182 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
183 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
184 |       } else {
185 |         if (scope.isGlobal()) {
186 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
187 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
188 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
189 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
190 |           } else {
191 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
192 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
193 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
194 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
195 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
196 |           }
197 |         } else {
198 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |         }
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseVariableDeclarations.GatherCollapses.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Method code:
136 |     @Override
137 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
138 |       if (n.isVar()) {
139 |         blacklistStubVars(t, n);
140 |       }
141 | 
142 |       // Only care about var nodes
143 |       if (!n.isVar() && !canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope())) return;
144 | 
145 |       // If we've already looked at this node, skip it
146 |       if (nodesToCollapse.contains(n)) return;
147 | 
148 |       // Adjacent VAR children of an IF node are the if and else parts and can't
149 |       // be collapsed
150 |       if (parent.isIf()) return;
151 | 
152 |       Node varNode = n;
153 | 
154 |       boolean hasVar = n.isVar();
155 | 
156 |       // Find variable declarations that follow this one (if any)
157 |       n = n.getNext();
158 | 
159 |       boolean hasNodesToCollapse = false;
160 | 
161 |       while (n != null &&
162 |           (n.isVar() || canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope()))) {
163 | 
164 |         if (n.isVar()) {
165 |           blacklistStubVars(t, n);
166 |           hasVar = true;
167 |         }
168 |

170 |         hasNodesToCollapse = true;
171 | 
172 |         n = n.getNext();
173 |       }
174 | 
175 |       if (hasNodesToCollapse && hasVar) {
176 |         nodesToCollapse.add(varNode);
177 |         collapses.add(new Collapse(varNode, n, parent));
178 |       }
179 |     }

===== M0145 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 170-279
Documentation:
/**
   * General cascading unused operation node removal.
   * @param n The root of the expression to simplify.
   * @param removeUnused If true, the node is removed from the AST if
   *     it is not useful, otherwise it replaced with an EMPTY node.
   * @return The replacement node, or null if the node was is not useful.
   */
Method code:
170 |   private Node trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node n, boolean removeUnused) {
171 |     Node result = n;
172 | 
173 |     // Simplify the results of conditional expressions
174 |     switch (n.getType()) {
175 |       case Token.HOOK:
176 |         Node trueNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild().getNext());
177 |         Node falseNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
178 |         // If one or more of the conditional children were removed,
179 |         // transform the HOOK to an equivalent operation:
180 |         //    x() ? foo() : 1 --> x() && foo()
181 |         //    x() ? 1 : foo() --> x() || foo()
182 |         //    x() ? 1 : 1 --> x()
183 |         //    x ? 1 : 1 --> null
184 |         if (trueNode == null && falseNode != null) {
185 |           n.setType(Token.OR);
186 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
187 |         } else if (trueNode != null && falseNode == null) {
188 |           n.setType(Token.AND);
189 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
190 |         } else if (trueNode == null && falseNode == null) {
191 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
192 |         } else {
193 |           // The structure didn't change.
194 |           result = n;
195 |         }
196 |         break;
197 |       case Token.AND:
198 |       case Token.OR:
199 |         // Try to remove the second operand from a AND or OR operations:
200 |         //    x() || f --> x()
201 |         //    x() && f --> x()
202 |         Node conditionalResultNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(
203 |             n.getLastChild());
204 |         if (conditionalResultNode == null) {
205 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
206 |           // The conditionally executed code was removed, so
207 |           // replace the AND/OR with its LHS or remove it if it isn't useful.
208 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
209 |         }
210 |         break;
211 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
212 |         // A function expression isn't useful if it isn't used, remove it and
213 |         // don't bother to look at its children.
214 |         result = null;
215 |         break;
216 |       case Token.COMMA:
217 |         // We rewrite other operations as COMMA expressions (which will later
218 |         // get split into individual EXPR_RESULT statement, if possible), so
219 |         // we special case COMMA (we don't want to rewrite COMMAs as new COMMAs
220 |         // nodes.
221 |         Node left = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
222 |         Node right = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
223 |         if (left == null && right == null) {
224 |           result = null;
225 |         } else if (left == null) {
226 |           result = right;
227 |         } else if (right == null){
228 |           result = left;
229 |         } else {
230 |           // The structure didn't change.
231 |           result = n;
232 |         }
233 |         break;
234 |       default:
235 |         if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
236 |           // This is the meat of this function. The node itself doesn't generate
237 |           // any side-effects but preserve any side-effects in the children.
238 |           Node resultList = null;
239 |           for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
240 |             next = c.getNext();
241 |             c = trySimplifyUnusedResult(c);
242 |             if (c != null) {
243 |               c.detachFromParent();
244 |               if (resultList == null)  {
245 |                 // The first side-effect can be used stand-alone.
246 |                 resultList = c;
247 |               } else {
248 |                 // Leave the side-effects in-place, simplifying it to a COMMA
249 |                 // expression.
250 |                 resultList = IR.comma(resultList, c).srcref(c);
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |           result = resultList;
255 |         }
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // Fix up the AST, replace or remove the an unused node (if requested).
259 |     if (n != result) {
260 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
261 |       if (result == null) {
262 |         if (removeUnused) {
263 |           parent.removeChild(n);
264 |         } else {
265 |           result = IR.empty().srcref(n);
266 |           parent.replaceChild(n, result);
267 |         }
268 |       } else {
269 |         // A new COMMA expression may not have an existing parent.
270 |         if (result.getParent() != null) {
271 |           result.detachFromParent();
272 |         }
273 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, result);
274 |       }
275 |       reportCodeChange();
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     return result;
279 |   }

===== M0156 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ExploitAssigns.collapseAssignEqualTo(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ExploitAssigns.java
Original range: 108-199
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse the given assign expression into the expression directly
   * following it, if possible.
   *
   * @param expr The expression that may be moved.
   * @param exprParent The parent of {@code expr}.
   * @param value The value of this expression, expressed as a node. Each
   *     expression may have multiple values, so this function may be called
   *     multiple times for the same expression. For example,
   *     <code>
   *     a = true;
   *     </code>
   *     is equal to the name "a" and the boolean "true".
   * @return Whether the expression was collapsed successfully.
   */
Method code:
108 |   private boolean collapseAssignEqualTo(Node expr, Node exprParent,
109 |       Node value) {
110 |     Node assign = expr.getFirstChild();
111 |     Node parent = exprParent;
112 |     Node next = expr.getNext();
113 |     while (next != null) {
114 |       switch (next.getType()) {
115 |         case Token.AND:
116 |         case Token.OR:
117 |         case Token.HOOK:
118 |         case Token.IF:
119 |         case Token.RETURN:
120 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
121 |           // Dive down the left side
122 |           parent = next;
123 |           next = next.getFirstChild();
124 |           break;
125 | 
126 |         case Token.VAR:
127 |           if (next.getFirstChild().hasChildren()) {
128 |             parent = next.getFirstChild();
129 |             next = parent.getFirstChild();
130 |             break;
131 |           }
132 |           return false;
133 | 
134 |         case Token.GETPROP:
135 |         case Token.NAME:
136 |           if (next.isQualifiedName()) {
137 |             String nextName = next.getQualifiedName();
138 |             if (value.isQualifiedName() &&
139 |                 nextName.equals(value.getQualifiedName())) {
140 |               // If the previous expression evaluates to value of a
141 |               // qualified name, and that qualified name is used again
142 |               // shortly, then we can exploit the assign here.
143 | 
144 |               // Verify the assignment doesn't change its own value.
145 |               if (!isSafeReplacement(next, assign)) {
146 |                 return false;
147 |               }
148 | 
149 |               exprParent.removeChild(expr);
150 |               expr.removeChild(assign);
151 |               parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
152 |               return true;
153 |             }
154 |           }
155 |           return false;
156 | 
157 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
158 |           // Assigns are really tricky. In lots of cases, we want to inline
159 |           // into the right side of the assign. But the left side of the
160 |           // assign is evaluated first, and it may have convoluted logic:
161 |           //   a = null;
162 |           //   (a = b).c = null;
163 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign. Similarly:
164 |           //   a.b = null;
165 |           //   a.b.c = null;
166 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign either.
167 |           //
168 |           // To protect against this, we simply only inline when the left side
169 |           // is guaranteed to evaluate to the same L-value no matter what.
170 |           Node leftSide = next.getFirstChild();
171 |           if (leftSide.isName() ||
172 |               leftSide.isGetProp() &&
173 |               leftSide.getFirstChild().isThis()) {
174 |             // Dive down the right side of the assign.
175 |             parent = next;
176 |             next = leftSide.getNext();
177 |             break;
178 |           } else {
179 |             return false;
180 |           }
181 | 
182 |         default:
183 |           if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(next)
184 |               && next.isEquivalentTo(value)) {
185 |             // If the r-value of the expr assign is an immutable value,
186 |             // and the value is used again shortly, then we can exploit
187 |             // the assign here.
188 |             exprParent.removeChild(expr);
189 |             expr.removeChild(assign);
190 |             parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
191 |             return true;
192 |           }
193 |           // Return without inlining a thing
194 |           return false;
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 | 
198 |     return false;
199 |   }

   * We treat this as the unknown type if any of its implicit prototype
   * properties is unknown.

Method code:
504 |   @Override
505 |   public boolean isUnknownType() {
506 |     // If the object is unknown now, check the supertype again,
507 |     // because it might have been resolved since the last check.
508 |     if (unknown) {
509 |       ObjectType implicitProto = getImplicitPrototype();

===== M0182 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeIf(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 633-865
Documentation:
/**
   * Try turning IF nodes into smaller HOOKs
   *
   * Returns the replacement for n or the original if no replacement was
   * necessary.
   */
Method code:
633 |   private Node tryMinimizeIf(Node n) {
634 | 
635 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
636 | 
637 |     Node cond = n.getFirstChild();
638 | 
639 |     /* If the condition is a literal, we'll let other
640 |      * optimizations try to remove useless code.
641 |      */
642 |     if (NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(cond, true)) {
643 |       return n;
644 |     }
645 | 
646 |     Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
647 |     Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
648 | 
649 |     if (elseBranch == null) {
650 |       if (isFoldableExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
651 |         Node expr = getBlockExpression(thenBranch);
652 |         if (!late && isPropertyAssignmentInExpression(expr)) {
653 |           // Keep opportunities for CollapseProperties such as
654 |           // a.longIdentifier || a.longIdentifier = ... -> var a = ...;
655 |           // until CollapseProperties has been run.
656 |           return n;
657 |         }
658 | 
659 |         if (cond.isNot()) {
660 |           // if(!x)bar(); -> x||bar();
661 |           if (isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(cond, OR_PRECEDENCE) &&
662 |               isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(expr.getFirstChild(),
663 |                   OR_PRECEDENCE)) {
664 |             // It's not okay to add two sets of parentheses.
665 |             return n;
666 |           }
667 | 
668 |           Node or = IR.or(
669 |               cond.removeFirstChild(),
670 |               expr.removeFirstChild()).srcref(n);
671 |           Node newExpr = NodeUtil.newExpr(or);
672 |           parent.replaceChild(n, newExpr);
673 |           reportCodeChange();
674 | 
675 |           return newExpr;
676 |         }
677 | 
678 |         // if(x)foo(); -> x&&foo();
679 |         if (isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(cond, AND_PRECEDENCE) &&
680 |             isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(expr.getFirstChild(),
681 |                 AND_PRECEDENCE)) {
682 |           // One additional set of parentheses is worth the change even if
683 |           // there is no immediate code size win. However, two extra pair of
684 |           // {}, we would have to think twice. (unless we know for sure the
685 |           // we can further optimize its parent.
686 |           return n;
687 |         }
688 | 
689 |         n.removeChild(cond);
690 |         Node and = IR.and(cond, expr.removeFirstChild()).srcref(n);
691 |         Node newExpr = NodeUtil.newExpr(and);
692 |         parent.replaceChild(n, newExpr);
693 |         reportCodeChange();
694 | 
695 |         return newExpr;
696 |       } else {
697 | 
698 |         // Try to combine two IF-ELSE
699 |         if (NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(thenBranch) &&
700 |             thenBranch.hasOneChild()) {
701 |           Node innerIf = thenBranch.getFirstChild();
702 | 
703 |           if (innerIf.isIf()) {
704 |             Node innerCond = innerIf.getFirstChild();
705 |             Node innerThenBranch = innerCond.getNext();
706 |             Node innerElseBranch = innerThenBranch.getNext();
707 | 
708 |             if (innerElseBranch == null &&
709 |                  !(isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(cond, AND_PRECEDENCE) &&
710 |                    isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(innerCond, AND_PRECEDENCE))) {
711 |               n.detachChildren();
712 |               n.addChildToBack(
713 |                   IR.and(
714 |                       cond,
715 |                       innerCond.detachFromParent())
716 |                       .srcref(cond));
717 |               n.addChildrenToBack(innerThenBranch.detachFromParent());
718 |               reportCodeChange();
719 |               // Not worth trying to fold the current IF-ELSE into && because
720 |               // the inner IF-ELSE wasn't able to be folded into && anyways.
721 |               return n;
722 |             }
723 |           }
724 |         }
725 |       }
726 | 
727 |       return n;
728 |     }
729 | 
730 |     /* TODO(dcc) This modifies the siblings of n, which is undesirable for a
731 |      * peephole optimization. This should probably get moved to another pass.
732 |      */
733 |     tryRemoveRepeatedStatements(n);
734 | 
735 |     // if(!x)foo();else bar(); -> if(x)bar();else foo();
736 |     // An additional set of curly braces isn't worth it.
737 |     if (cond.isNot() && !consumesDanglingElse(elseBranch)) {
738 |       n.replaceChild(cond, cond.removeFirstChild());
739 |       n.removeChild(thenBranch);
740 |       n.addChildToBack(thenBranch);
741 |       reportCodeChange();
742 |       return n;
743 |     }
744 | 
745 |     // if(x)return 1;else return 2; -> return x?1:2;
746 |     if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpressBlock(elseBranch)) {
747 |       Node thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
748 |       Node elseExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(elseBranch);
749 |       n.removeChild(cond);
750 |       thenExpr.detachFromParent();
751 |       elseExpr.detachFromParent();
752 | 
753 |       // note - we ignore any cases with "return;", technically this
754 |       // can be converted to "return undefined;" or some variant, but
755 |       // that does not help code size.
756 |       Node returnNode = IR.returnNode(
757 |                             IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
758 |                                 .srcref(n));
759 |       parent.replaceChild(n, returnNode);
760 |       reportCodeChange();
761 |       return returnNode;
762 |     }
763 | 
764 |     boolean thenBranchIsExpressionBlock = isFoldableExpressBlock(thenBranch);
765 |     boolean elseBranchIsExpressionBlock = isFoldableExpressBlock(elseBranch);
766 | 
767 |     if (thenBranchIsExpressionBlock && elseBranchIsExpressionBlock) {
768 |       Node thenOp = getBlockExpression(thenBranch).getFirstChild();
769 |       Node elseOp = getBlockExpression(elseBranch).getFirstChild();
770 |       if (thenOp.getType() == elseOp.getType()) {
771 |         // if(x)a=1;else a=2; -> a=x?1:2;
772 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(thenOp)) {
773 |           Node lhs = thenOp.getFirstChild();
774 |           if (areNodesEqualForInlining(lhs, elseOp.getFirstChild()) &&
775 |               // if LHS has side effects, don't proceed [since the optimization
776 |               // evaluates LHS before cond]
777 |               // NOTE - there are some circumstances where we can
778 |               // proceed even if there are side effects...
779 |               !mayEffectMutableState(lhs)) {
780 | 
781 |             n.removeChild(cond);
782 |             Node assignName = thenOp.removeFirstChild();
783 |             Node thenExpr = thenOp.removeFirstChild();
784 |             Node elseExpr = elseOp.getLastChild();
785 |             elseOp.removeChild(elseExpr);
786 | 
787 |             Node hookNode = IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr).srcref(n);
788 |             Node assign = new Node(thenOp.getType(), assignName, hookNode)
789 |                               .srcref(thenOp);
790 |             Node expr = NodeUtil.newExpr(assign);
791 |             parent.replaceChild(n, expr);
792 |             reportCodeChange();
793 | 
794 |             return expr;
795 |           }
796 |         }
797 |       }
798 |       // if(x)foo();else bar(); -> x?foo():bar()
799 |       n.removeChild(cond);
800 |       thenOp.detachFromParent();
801 |       elseOp.detachFromParent();
802 |       Node expr = IR.exprResult(
803 |           IR.hook(cond, thenOp, elseOp).srcref(n));
804 |       parent.replaceChild(n, expr);
805 |       reportCodeChange();
806 |       return expr;
807 |     }
808 | 
809 |     boolean thenBranchIsVar = isVarBlock(thenBranch);
810 |     boolean elseBranchIsVar = isVarBlock(elseBranch);
811 | 
812 |     // if(x)var y=1;else y=2  ->  var y=x?1:2
813 |     if (thenBranchIsVar && elseBranchIsExpressionBlock &&
814 |         getBlockExpression(elseBranch).getFirstChild().isAssign()) {
815 | 
816 |       Node var = getBlockVar(thenBranch);
817 |       Node elseAssign = getBlockExpression(elseBranch).getFirstChild();
818 | 
819 |       Node name1 = var.getFirstChild();
820 |       Node maybeName2 = elseAssign.getFirstChild();
821 | 
822 |       if (name1.hasChildren()
823 |           && maybeName2.isName()
824 |           && name1.getString().equals(maybeName2.getString())) {
825 |         Node thenExpr = name1.removeChildren();
826 |         Node elseExpr = elseAssign.getLastChild().detachFromParent();
827 |         cond.detachFromParent();
828 |         Node hookNode = IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
829 |                             .srcref(n);
830 |         var.detachFromParent();
831 |         name1.addChildrenToBack(hookNode);
832 |         parent.replaceChild(n, var);
833 |         reportCodeChange();
834 |         return var;
835 |       }
836 | 
837 |     // if(x)y=1;else var y=2  ->  var y=x?1:2
838 |     } else if (elseBranchIsVar && thenBranchIsExpressionBlock &&
839 |         getBlockExpression(thenBranch).getFirstChild().isAssign()) {
840 | 
841 |       Node var = getBlockVar(elseBranch);
842 |       Node thenAssign = getBlockExpression(thenBranch).getFirstChild();
843 | 
844 |       Node maybeName1 = thenAssign.getFirstChild();
845 |       Node name2 = var.getFirstChild();
846 | 
847 |       if (name2.hasChildren()
848 |           && maybeName1.isName()
849 |           && maybeName1.getString().equals(name2.getString())) {
850 |         Node thenExpr = thenAssign.getLastChild().detachFromParent();
851 |         Node elseExpr = name2.removeChildren();
852 |         cond.detachFromParent();
853 |         Node hookNode = IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
854 |                             .srcref(n);
855 |         var.detachFromParent();
856 |         name2.addChildrenToBack(hookNode);
857 |         parent.replaceChild(n, var);

84 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
85 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.

88 |     // so we'll allow it.

99 |     // these cases when we visit the child, and the peephole passes will
100 |     // fix up the tree in more clever ways when these are removed.
101 |     if (n.isExprResult() || n.isBlock()) {

103 |     }

108 |       return;

115 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
116 |       if (n.isString()) {

120 |             "' operator is not being used.";
121 |       }

===== M0193 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 591-628
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * the name a is not.
   *
   * Function literals do not meet this definition, because they
   * lexically capture variables. For example, if you have
   * <code>
   * function() { return a; }
   * </code>
   * If it is evaluated in a different scope, then it
   * captures a different variable. Even if the function did not read
   * any captured variables directly, it would still fail this definition,
   * because it affects the lifecycle of variables in the enclosing scope.
   *
   * However, a function literal with respect to a particular scope is
   * a literal.
   *
   * @param includeFunctions If true, all function expressions will be
   *     treated as literals.
   */
Method code:
591 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n, boolean includeFunctions) {
592 |     switch (n.getType()) {
593 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
594 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
595 |              child = child.getNext()) {
596 |           if ((!child.isEmpty()) && !isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
597 |             return false;
598 |           }
599 |         }
600 |         return true;
601 | 
602 |       case Token.REGEXP:
603 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
604 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
605 |              child = child.getNext()) {
606 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
607 |             return false;
608 |           }
609 |         }
610 |         return true;
611 | 
612 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
613 |         // Return true only if all values are const.
614 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
615 |              child = child.getNext()) {
616 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions)) {
617 |             return false;
618 |           }
619 |         }
620 |         return true;
621 | 
622 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
623 |         return includeFunctions && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n);
624 | 
625 |       default:
626 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
627 |     }
628 |   }

     * If this is an assign to a variable or its property, return it.

919 |     static Assign maybeCreateAssign(Node assignNode) {
920 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(assignNode));
921 | 
922 |       // Skip one level of GETPROPs or GETELEMs.
923 |       //
924 |       // Don't skip more than one level, because then we get into

944 |       return null;

===== M0234 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.java
Original range: 35-82
Documentation:

Method code:
35 |   @Override
36 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
37 |     if (!subtree.isScript() && !subtree.isBlock()) {
38 |       return subtree;
39 |     }
40 | 
41 |     boolean codeChanged = false;
42 | 
43 |     // Look for variable declarations or simple assignments
44 |     // and start processing there.
45 |     for (Node child = subtree.getFirstChild();
46 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
47 |       if (!child.isVar() && !NodeUtil.isExprAssign(child)) {
48 |         continue;
49 |       }
50 |       if (!isPropertyAssignmentToName(child.getNext())) {
51 |         // Quick check to see if there's anything to collapse.
52 |         continue;
53 |       }
54 | 
55 |       Preconditions.checkState(child.hasOneChild());
56 |       Node name = getName(child);
57 |       if (!name.isName()) {
58 |         // The assignment target is not a simple name.
59 |         continue;
60 |       }
61 |       Node value = getValue(child);
62 |       if (value == null || !isInterestingValue(value)) {
63 |         // No initializer or not an Object or Array literal.
64 |         continue;
65 |       }
66 | 
67 |       Node propertyCandidate;
68 |       while ((propertyCandidate = child.getNext()) != null) {
69 |         // This does not infinitely loop because collectProperty always
70 |         // removes propertyCandidate from its parent when it returns true.
71 |         if (!collectProperty(propertyCandidate, name.getString(), value)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |         codeChanged = true;
75 |       }
76 |     }
77 | 
78 |     if (codeChanged) {
79 |       reportCodeChange();
80 |     }
81 |     return subtree;
82 |   }

/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in

     * unquoted.

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphColoring.GreedyGraphColoring.color()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/GraphColoring.java

Method code:
130 |     @Override
131 |     public int color() {
132 |       graph.clearNodeAnnotations();
133 |       List<GraphNode<N, E>> worklist = Lists.newArrayList(graph.getNodes());
134 | 
135 |       // Sort nodes by degree.
136 |       Collections.sort(worklist, new Comparator<GraphNode<N, E>>() {
137 |         @Override
138 |         public int compare(GraphNode<N, E> o1, GraphNode<N, E> o2) {
139 |           int result = graph.getWeight(o2.getValue())
140 |               - graph.getWeight(o1.getValue());
141 |           return result == 0 && tieBreaker != null ?
142 |               tieBreaker.compare(o1.getValue(), o2.getValue()) : result;
143 |         }
144 |       });
145 | 
146 |       // Idea: From the highest to lowest degree, assign any uncolored node with
147 |       // a unique color if none of its neighbor has been assigned that color.
148 |       int count = 0;
149 |       do {
150 |         Color color = new Color(count);
151 |         SubGraph<N, E> subgraph = graph.newSubGraph();
152 |         for (Iterator<GraphNode<N, E>> i = worklist.iterator(); i.hasNext();) {
153 |           GraphNode<N, E> node = i.next();
154 |           if (subgraph.isIndependentOf(node.getValue())) {
155 |             subgraph.addNode(node.getValue());
156 |             node.setAnnotation(color);
157 |             i.remove();
158 |           }
159 |         }
160 |         count++;
161 |       } while (!worklist.isEmpty());
162 |       @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
163 |       N[] map = (N[]) new Object[count];
164 |       colorToNodeMap = map;
165 |       return count;
166 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.trySplitComma(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 272-298
Documentation:

Method code:
272 |   private Node trySplitComma(Node n) {
273 |     if (late) {
274 |       return n;
275 |     }
276 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
277 |     Node left = n.getFirstChild();
278 |     Node right = n.getLastChild();
279 | 
280 |     if (parent.isExprResult()
281 |         && !parent.getParent().isLabel()) {
282 |       // split comma
283 |       n.detachChildren();
284 |       // Replace the original expression with the left operand.
285 |       parent.replaceChild(n, left);
286 |       // Add the right expression afterward.
287 |       Node newStatement = IR.exprResult(right);
288 |       newStatement.copyInformationFrom(n);
289 | 
290 |       //This modifies outside the subtree, which is not
291 |       //desirable in a peephole optimization.
292 |       parent.getParent().addChildAfter(newStatement, parent);
293 |       reportCodeChange();
294 |       return left;
295 |     } else {
296 |       return n;
297 |     }
298 |   }

===== M0271 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.SortedDependencies.topologicalStableSort(List<T>,Multimap<T, T>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/SortedDependencies.java
Original range: 239-288
Documentation:

Method code:
239 |   private static <T> List<T> topologicalStableSort(
240 |       List<T> items, Multimap<T, T> deps) {
241 |     if (items.size() == 0) {
242 |       // Priority queue blows up if we give it a size of 0. Since we need
243 |       // to special case this either way, just bail out.
244 |       return Lists.newArrayList();
245 |     }
246 | 
247 |     final Map<T, Integer> originalIndex = Maps.newHashMap();
248 |     for (int i = 0; i < items.size(); i++) {
249 |       originalIndex.put(items.get(i), i);
250 |     }
251 | 
252 |     PriorityQueue<T> inDegreeZero = new PriorityQueue<T>(items.size(),
253 |         new Comparator<T>() {
254 |       @Override
255 |       public int compare(T a, T b) {
256 |         return originalIndex.get(a).intValue() -
257 |             originalIndex.get(b).intValue();
258 |       }
259 |     });
260 |     List<T> result = Lists.newArrayList();
261 | 
262 |     Multiset<T> inDegree = HashMultiset.create();
263 |     Multimap<T, T> reverseDeps = ArrayListMultimap.create();
264 |     Multimaps.invertFrom(deps, reverseDeps);
265 | 
266 |     // First, add all the inputs with in-degree 0.
267 |     for (T item : items) {
268 |       Collection<T> itemDeps = deps.get(item);
269 |       inDegree.add(item, itemDeps.size());
270 |       if (itemDeps.isEmpty()) {
271 |         inDegreeZero.add(item);
272 |       }
273 |     }
274 | 
275 |     // Then, iterate to a fixed point over the reverse dependency graph.
276 |     while (!inDegreeZero.isEmpty()) {
277 |       T item = inDegreeZero.remove();
278 |       result.add(item);
279 |       for (T inWaiting : reverseDeps.get(item)) {
280 |         inDegree.remove(inWaiting, 1);
281 |         if (inDegree.count(inWaiting) == 0) {
282 |           inDegreeZero.add(inWaiting);
283 |         }
284 |       }
285 |     }
286 | 
287 |     return result;
288 |   }

===== M0306 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 124-170
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function
   * except it return UNKNOWN for known values with side-effects, use
   * getExpressionBooleanValue if you don't care about side-effects.
   */
Method code:
124 |   static TernaryValue getPureBooleanValue(Node n) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.STRING:
127 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getString().length() > 0);
128 | 
129 |       case Token.NUMBER:
130 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getDouble() != 0);
131 | 
132 |       case Token.NOT:
133 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild()).not();
134 | 
135 |       case Token.NULL:
136 |       case Token.FALSE:
137 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
138 | 
139 |       case Token.VOID:
140 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n.getFirstChild())) {
141 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
142 |         }
143 |         break;
144 | 
145 |       case Token.NAME:
146 |         String name = n.getString();
147 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
148 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
149 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
150 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
151 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
152 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
153 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
154 |         }
155 |         break;
156 | 
157 |       case Token.TRUE:
158 |       case Token.REGEXP:
159 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
160 | 
161 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
162 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
163 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
164 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
165 |         }
166 |         break;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
170 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.StatementFusion.fuseIntoOneStatement(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/StatementFusion.java
Original range: 85-119
Documentation:

Method code:
85 |   private void fuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
86 |     Node cur = block.removeFirstChild();
87 | 
88 |     // Starts building a tree.
89 |     Node commaTree = cur.removeFirstChild();
90 | 
91 | 
92 |     while (block.hasMoreThanOneChild()) {
93 |       Node next = block.removeFirstChild().removeFirstChild();
94 |       commaTree = fuseExpressionIntoExpression(commaTree, next);
95 |     }
96 | 
97 |     Preconditions.checkState(block.hasOneChild());
98 |     Node last = block.getLastChild();
99 | 
100 |     // Now we are just left with two statements. The comma tree of the first
101 |     // n - 1 statements (which can be used in an expression) and the last
102 |     // statement. We perform specific fusion based on the last statement's type.
103 |     switch(last.getType()) {
104 |       case Token.IF:
105 |       case Token.RETURN:
106 |       case Token.THROW:
107 |       case Token.SWITCH:
108 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
109 |         fuseExpresssonIntoFirstChild(commaTree, last);
110 |         return;
111 |       case Token.FOR:
112 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(last)) {
113 |           fuseExpresssonIntoSecondChild(commaTree, last);
114 |         }
115 |         return ;
116 |       default:
117 |         throw new IllegalStateException("Statement fusion missing.");
118 |     }
119 |   }

388 |       // It's important that this ordering is deterministic, so that
389 |       // multiple compiles with the same input produce exactly the same

392 |       // To do this, grab any passes we recognize, and move them to the end

401 |         }
402 |       }
403 |

===== M0374 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1686-1727
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1686 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1687 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1688 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1689 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1690 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1691 |       // {?} - right curly
1692 |       // {?=} - equals
1693 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1694 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1695 |       // {function(number, ...[?])} - right bracket
1696 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1697 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1698 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1699 |       token = next();
1700 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1701 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1702 |           token == JsDocToken.RB ||
1703 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1704 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1705 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE) {
1706 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1707 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1708 |       }
1709 | 
1710 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1711 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1712 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1713 |     } else {
1714 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1715 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1716 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1717 |           next();
1718 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1719 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1720 |           next();
1721 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1722 |         }
1723 |       }
1724 | 
1725 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1726 |     }
1727 |   }

252 |             NodeUtil.isConstantByConvention(
253 |                 compiler.getCodingConvention(), n, parent);
254 |         boolean isMarkedConstant = n.getBooleanProp(Node.IS_CONSTANT_NAME);
255 |         if (shouldBeConstant && !isMarkedConstant) {

257 |             String name = n.getString();
258 |             throw new IllegalStateException(

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CompilerOptions.getReplacementsHelper(Map<String, Object>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CompilerOptions.java
Original range: 952-970
Documentation:
/**
   * Creates a map of String->Node from a map of String->Number/String/Boolean.
   */
Method code:
952 |   private static Map<String, Node> getReplacementsHelper(
953 |       Map<String, Object> source) {
954 |     Map<String, Node> map = Maps.newHashMap();
955 |     for (Map.Entry<String, Object> entry : source.entrySet()) {
956 |       String name = entry.getKey();
957 |       Object value = entry.getValue();
958 |       if (value instanceof Boolean) {
959 |         map.put(name, NodeUtil.booleanNode(((Boolean) value).booleanValue()));
960 |       } else if (value instanceof Integer) {
961 |         map.put(name, IR.number(((Integer) value).intValue()));
962 |       } else if (value instanceof Double) {
963 |         map.put(name, IR.number(((Double) value).doubleValue()));
964 |       } else {
965 |         Preconditions.checkState(value instanceof String);
966 |         map.put(name, IR.string((String) value));
967 |       }
968 |     }
969 |     return map;
970 |   }

129 |     private boolean isVarInlineForbidden(Var var) {
130 |       // A variable may not be inlined if:
131 |       // 1) The variable is defined in the externs

Method code:
423 |     @Override
424 |     public Bind describeFunctionBind(Node n, boolean useTypeInfo) {
425 |       if (!n.isCall()) {
426 |         return null;
427 |       }
428 | 
429 |       Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
430 |       String name = callTarget.getQualifiedName();
431 |       if (name != null) {
432 |         if (name.equals("Function.prototype.bind.call")) {
433 |           // goog.bind(fn, self, args...);
434 |           Node fn = callTarget.getNext();
435 |           if (fn == null) {
436 |             return null;
437 |           }
438 |           Node thisValue = safeNext(fn);
439 |           Node parameters = safeNext(thisValue);
440 |           return new Bind(fn, thisValue, parameters);
441 |         }
442 |       }
443 | 
444 |       if (callTarget.isGetProp()
445 |           && callTarget.getLastChild().getString().equals("bind")) {
446 |         Node maybeFn = callTarget.getFirstChild();
447 |         JSType maybeFnType = maybeFn.getJSType();
448 |         FunctionType fnType = null;
449 |         if (useTypeInfo && maybeFnType != null) {
450 |           fnType = maybeFnType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined()
451 |               .toMaybeFunctionType();
452 |         }
453 | 
454 |         if (fnType != null || maybeFn.isFunction()) {
455 |           // (function(){}).bind(self, args...);
456 |           Node thisValue = callTarget.getNext();
457 |           Node parameters = safeNext(thisValue);
458 |           return new Bind(maybeFn, thisValue, parameters);
459 |         }
460 |       }
461 | 
462 |       return null;
463 |     }

===== M0419 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MustBeReachingVariableDef.computeMustDef(Node,Node,MustDef,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MustBeReachingVariableDef.java
Original range: 225-318
Documentation:
/**
   * @param n The node in question.
   * @param cfgNode The node to add
   * @param conditional true if the definition is not always executed.
   */
Method code:
225 |   private void computeMustDef(
226 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, MustDef output, boolean conditional) {
227 |     switch (n.getType()) {
228 | 
229 |       case Token.BLOCK:
230 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
231 |         return;
232 | 
233 |       case Token.WHILE:
234 |       case Token.DO:
235 |       case Token.IF:
236 |         computeMustDef(
237 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
238 |         return;
239 | 
240 |       case Token.FOR:
241 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
242 |           computeMustDef(
243 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
244 |         } else {
245 |           // for(x in y) {...}
246 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
247 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
248 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
249 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
250 |           }
251 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
252 |             addToDefIfLocal(lhs.getString(), cfgNode, rhs, output);
253 |           }
254 |         }
255 |         return;
256 | 
257 |       case Token.AND:
258 |       case Token.OR:
259 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
260 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
261 |         return;
262 | 
263 |       case Token.HOOK:
264 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
265 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
266 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
267 |         return;
268 | 
269 |       case Token.VAR:
270 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
271 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
272 |             computeMustDef(c.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
273 |             addToDefIfLocal(c.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
274 |                 c.getFirstChild(), output);
275 |           }
276 |         }
277 |         return;
278 | 
279 |       default:
280 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
281 |           if (n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
282 |             Node name = n.getFirstChild();
283 |             computeMustDef(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
284 |             addToDefIfLocal(name.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
285 |               n.getLastChild(), output);
286 |             return;
287 |           } else if (NodeUtil.isGet(n.getFirstChild())) {
288 |             // Treat all assignments to arguments as redefining the
289 |             // parameters itself.
290 |             Node obj = n.getFirstChild().getFirstChild();
291 |             if (obj.isName() && "arguments".equals(obj.getString())) {
292 |               // TODO(user): More accuracy can be introduced
293 |               // i.e. We know exactly what arguments[x] is if x is a constant
294 |               // number.
295 |               escapeParameters(output);
296 |             }
297 |           }
298 |         }
299 | 
300 |         if (n.isName() && "arguments".equals(n.getString())) {
301 |           escapeParameters(output);
302 |         }
303 | 
304 |         // DEC and INC actually defines the variable.
305 |         if (n.isDec() || n.isInc()) {
306 |           Node target = n.getFirstChild();
307 |           if (target.isName()) {
308 |             addToDefIfLocal(target.getString(),
309 |                 conditional ? null : cfgNode, null, output);
310 |             return;
311 |           }
312 |         }
313 | 
314 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
315 |           computeMustDef(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
316 |         }
317 |     }
318 |   }

===== M0420 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessClosurePrimitives.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessClosurePrimitives.java
Original range: 172-259
Documentation:

Method code:
172 |   @Override
173 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
174 |     switch (n.getType()) {
175 |       case Token.CALL:
176 |         boolean isExpr = parent.isExprResult();
177 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
178 |         if (left.isGetProp()) {
179 |           Node name = left.getFirstChild();
180 |           if (name.isName() &&
181 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
182 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
183 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
184 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
185 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
186 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
187 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
188 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
189 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
190 |               break;
191 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
192 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
193 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
194 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
195 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
196 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
197 |               if (arg.isString()) {
198 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
199 |                 if (dot == -1) {
200 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
201 |                 } else {
202 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
203 |                 }
204 |               }
205 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
206 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
207 |               List<String> typeDecls =
208 |                   convention.identifyTypeDeclarationCall(n);
209 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
210 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
211 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
212 |                 }
213 |               }
214 | 
215 |               // We can't modify parent, so just create a node that will
216 |               // get compiled out.
217 |               parent.replaceChild(n, IR.number(0));
218 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
219 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
220 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
221 |             }
222 |           }
223 |         }
224 |         break;
225 | 
226 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
227 |       case Token.NAME:
228 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
229 |         // object.
230 |         handleCandidateProvideDefinition(t, n, parent);
231 |         break;
232 | 
233 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
234 |         handleTypedefDefinition(t, n, parent);
235 |         break;
236 | 
237 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
238 |         // If this is a declaration of a provided named function, this is an
239 |         // error. Hoisted functions will explode if they're provided.
240 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&
241 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
242 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
243 |           ProvidedName pn = providedNames.get(name);
244 |           if (pn != null) {
245 |             compiler.report(t.makeError(n, FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_ERROR, name));
246 |           }
247 |         }
248 |         break;
249 | 
250 |       case Token.GETPROP:
251 |         if (n.getFirstChild().isName() &&
252 |             !parent.isCall() &&
253 |             !parent.isAssign() &&
254 |             "goog.base".equals(n.getQualifiedName())) {
255 |           reportBadBaseClassUse(t, n, "May only be called directly.");
256 |         }
257 |         break;
258 |     }
259 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 500-541
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempt to replace the condition of if or hook immediately that is a
   * reference to a name that is assigned immediately before.
   */
Method code:
500 |   private void tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node n) {
501 |     Node next = n.getNext();
502 | 
503 |     // Look for patterns like the following and replace the if-condition with
504 |     // a constant value so it can later be folded:
505 |     //   var a = /a/;
506 |     //   if (a) {foo(a)}
507 |     // or
508 |     //   a = 0;
509 |     //   a ? foo(a) : c;
510 |     // or
511 |     //   a = 0;
512 |     //   a || foo(a);
513 |     // or
514 |     //   a = 0;
515 |     //   a && foo(a)
516 |     //
517 |     // TODO(johnlenz): This would be better handled by control-flow sensitive
518 |     // constant propagation. As the other case that I want to handle is:
519 |     //   i=0; for(;i<0;i++){}
520 |     // as right now nothing facilitates removing a loop like that.
521 |     // This is here simply to remove the cruft left behind goog.userAgent and
522 |     // similar cases.
523 | 
524 |     if (isSimpleAssignment(n) && isConditionalStatement(next)) {
525 |       Node lhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentName(n);
526 | 
527 |       Node condition = getConditionalStatementCondition(next);
528 |       if (lhsAssign.isName() && condition.isName()
529 |           && lhsAssign.getString().equals(condition.getString())) {
530 |         Node rhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentValue(n);
531 |         TernaryValue value = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(rhsAssign);
532 |         if (value != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
533 |           Node replacementConditionNode =
534 |               NodeUtil.booleanNode(value.toBoolean(true));
535 |           condition.getParent().replaceChild(condition,
536 |               replacementConditionNode);
537 |           reportCodeChange();
538 |         }
539 |       }
540 |     }
541 |   }

===== M0483 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.computeEscaped(Scope,Set<Var>,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 548-578
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in JavaScript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */
Method code:
548 |   static void computeEscaped(final Scope jsScope, final Set<Var> escaped,
549 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {
550 |     // TODO(user): Very good place to store this information somewhere.
551 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {
552 |       @Override
553 |       public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
554 |         if (jsScope == t.getScope() || !n.isName()
555 |             || parent.isFunction()) {
556 |           return;
557 |         }
558 |         String name = n.getString();
559 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
560 |         if (var != null && var.scope == jsScope) {
561 |           escaped.add(jsScope.getVar(name));
562 |         }
563 |       }
564 |     };
565 | 
566 |     NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, finder);
567 |     t.traverseAtScope(jsScope);
568 | 
569 |     // 1: Remove the exception name in CATCH which technically isn't local to
570 |     //    begin with.
571 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = jsScope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
572 |       Var var = i.next();
573 |       if (var.getParentNode().isCatch() ||
574 |           compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.getName())) {
575 |         escaped.add(var);
576 |       }
577 |     }
578 |   }

===== M0489 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1910 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1911 |     return n.isFunction() && !isStatement(n);
1912 |   }

86 |     // at least one inner function because in most browsers, when there is a
87 |     // closure, ALL the variables are saved (escaped).
88 |     Node fnBlock = t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild();
89 |     if (NodeUtil.containsFunction(fnBlock)) {
90 |       return;
91 |     }
92 | 
93 |     // We don't do any dead assignment elimination if there are no assigns
94 |     // to eliminate. :)
95 |     if (!NodeUtil.has(fnBlock, matchRemovableAssigns,
96 |             Predicates.<Node>alwaysTrue())) {
97 |       return;
98 |     }
99 | 
100 |     // Computes liveness information first.
101 |     ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg = t.getControlFlowGraph();
102 |     liveness = new LiveVariablesAnalysis(cfg, scope, compiler);
103 |     liveness.analyze();
104 |     tryRemoveDeadAssignments(t, cfg);
105 |   }

153 |   LiveVariableLattice flowThrough(Node node, LiveVariableLattice input) {
154 |     final BitSet gen = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
155 |     final BitSet kill = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
156 | 
157 |     // Make kills conditional if the node can end abruptly by an exception.
158 |     boolean conditional = false;
159 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> edgeList = getCfg().getOutEdges(node);
160 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> edge : edgeList) {

162 |         conditional = true;
163 |       }

167 |     // L_in = L_out - Kill + Gen

52 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {

54 |     if (gNode != null && gNode.getAnnotation() != GraphReachability.REACHABLE) {

59 |   final JsDocToken getJsDocToken() {

88 |             }
89 |           } while (true);
90 | 
91 |         case '*':
92 |           if (matchChar('/')) {
93 |             return JsDocToken.EOC;
94 |           } else {
95 |             return JsDocToken.STAR;
96 |           }

98 |         case ',':
99 |           return JsDocToken.COMMA;
100 | 
101 |         case '>':
102 |           return JsDocToken.GT;
103 | 
104 |         case '(':
105 |           return JsDocToken.LP;
106 | 
107 |         case ')':
108 |           return JsDocToken.RP;
109 | 
110 |         case '{':
111 |           return JsDocToken.LC;
112 | 
113 |         case '}':
114 |           return JsDocToken.RC;
115 | 
116 |         case '[':
117 |           return JsDocToken.LB;
118 | 
119 |         case ']':
120 |           return JsDocToken.RB;
121 | 
122 |         case '?':
123 |           return JsDocToken.QMARK;
124 | 
125 |         case '!':
126 |           return JsDocToken.BANG;
127 | 
128 |         case ':':
129 |           return JsDocToken.COLON;
130 | 
131 |         case '=':
132 |           return JsDocToken.EQUALS;
133 | 
134 |         case '|':
135 |           matchChar('|');
136 |           return JsDocToken.PIPE;
137 | 
138 |         case '.':
139 |           c = getChar();

141 |             return JsDocToken.LT;
142 |           } else {
143 |             if (c == '.') {
144 |               c = getChar();
145 |               if (c == '.') {

175 |                 this.string = getStringFromBuffer();

177 |                 return JsDocToken.STRING;
178 |               } else {

181 |                 } else {
182 |                   ungetChar(c2);
183 |                   addToString(c1);
184 |                   this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
185 |                   stringBufferTop = 0;
186 |                   return JsDocToken.STRING;
