/**
   * Returns true if calls to this function have side effects.
   *
   * @param callNode The call node to inspected.
   * @param compiler A compiler object to provide program state changing
   *     context information. Can be null.
   */
Method code:
994 |   static boolean functionCallHasSideEffects(
995 |       Node callNode, @Nullable AbstractCompiler compiler) {
996 |     if (!callNode.isCall()) {
997 |       throw new IllegalStateException(
998 |           "Expected CALL node, got " + Token.name(callNode.getType()));
999 |     }
1000 | 
1001 |     if (callNode.isNoSideEffectsCall()) {
1002 |       return false;
1003 |     }
1004 | 
1005 |     Node nameNode = callNode.getFirstChild();
1006 | 
1007 |     // Built-in functions with no side effects.
1008 |     if (nameNode.isName()) {
1009 |       String name = nameNode.getString();
1010 |       if (BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS_WITHOUT_SIDEEFFECTS.contains(name)) {
1011 |         return false;
1012 |       }
1013 |     } else if (nameNode.isGetProp()) {
1014 |       if (callNode.hasOneChild()
1015 |           && OBJECT_METHODS_WITHOUT_SIDEEFFECTS.contains(
1016 |                 nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1017 |         return false;
1018 |       }
1019 | 
1020 |       if (callNode.isOnlyModifiesThisCall()
1021 |           && evaluatesToLocalValue(nameNode.getFirstChild())) {
1022 |         return false;
1023 |       }
1024 | 
1025 |       // Math.floor has no side-effects.
1026 |       // TODO(nicksantos): This is a terrible terrible hack, until
1027 |       // I create a definitionProvider that understands namespacing.
1028 |       if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isName()) {
1029 |         if ("Math.floor".equals(nameNode.getQualifiedName())) {
1030 |           return false;
1031 |         }
1032 |       }
1033 | 
1034 |       if (compiler != null && !compiler.hasRegExpGlobalReferences()) {
1035 |         if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isRegExp()
1036 |             && REGEXP_METHODS.contains(nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1037 |           return false;
1038 |         } else if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isString()
1039 |             && STRING_REGEXP_METHODS.contains(
1040 |                 nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1041 |           Node param = nameNode.getNext();
1042 |           if (param != null &&
1043 |               (param.isString() || param.isRegExp()))
1044 |           return false;
1045 |         }
1046 |       }
1047 |     }
1048 | 
1049 |     return true;
1050 |   }

/**
     * Updates our representation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name's longest prefix before the "prototype" property if the
     * name includes the "prototype" property. Does nothing otherwise.
     *
     * @param t The current node traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return Whether the name was handled
     */
Method code:
766 |     boolean maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent,
767 |         String name) {
768 |       // We use a string-based approach instead of inspecting the parse tree
769 |       // to avoid complexities with object literals, possibly nested, beneath
770 |       // assignments.
771 | 
772 |       int numLevelsToRemove;
773 |       String prefix;
774 |       if (name.endsWith(".prototype")) {
775 |         numLevelsToRemove = 1;
776 |         prefix = name.substring(0, name.length() - 10);
777 |       } else {
778 |         int i = name.indexOf(".prototype.");
779 |         if (i == -1) {
780 |           return false;
781 |         }
782 |         prefix = name.substring(0, i);
783 |         numLevelsToRemove = 2;
784 |         i = name.indexOf('.', i + 11);
785 |         while (i >= 0) {
786 |           numLevelsToRemove++;
787 |           i = name.indexOf('.', i + 1);
788 |         }
789 |       }
790 | 
791 |       if (parent != null && NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
792 |         // Object literal keys have no prefix that's referenced directly per
793 |         // key, so we're done.
794 |         return true;
795 |       }
796 | 
797 |       for (int i = 0; i < numLevelsToRemove; i++) {
798 |         parent = n;
799 |         n = n.getFirstChild();
800 |       }
801 | 
802 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, prefix, Ref.Type.PROTOTYPE_GET);
803 |       return true;
804 |     }

113 |   private void traverse(Node node) {
114 |     // The goal here is to avoid retraversing
115 |     // the entire AST to catch newly created opportunities.
116 |     // So we track whether a "unit of code" has changed,
117 |     // and revisit immediately.
118 |     if (!shouldVisit(node)) {
119 |       return;
120 |     }
121 | 
122 |     int visits = 0;
123 |     do {
124 |       Node c = node.getFirstChild();
125 |       while(c != null) {
126 |         traverse(c);
127 |         Node next = c.getNext();
128 |         c = next;
129 |       }
130 | 
131 |       visit(node);
132 |       visits++;
133 | 
134 |       Preconditions.checkState(visits < 10000, "too many interations");
135 |     } while (shouldRetraverse(node));
136 | 
137 |     exitNode(node);
138 |   }

1529 |         if (quoted1 != quoted2) {
1530 |           return false;
1531 |         }
1532 |       }
1533 |

1535 |       int slashV2 = node.getIntProp(SLASH_V);
1536 |       if (slashV1 != slashV2) {
1537 |         return false;
1538 |       }
1539 |     } else if (type == Token.CALL) {
1540 |       if (this.getBooleanProp(FREE_CALL) != node.getBooleanProp(FREE_CALL)) {
1541 |         return false;
1542 |       }
1543 |     }
1544 | 
1545 |     if (recurse) {
1546 |       Node n, n2;
1547 |       for (n = first, n2 = node.first;
1548 |            n != null;

1550 |         if (!n.isEquivalentTo(n2, compareJsType, true)) {
1551 |           return false;
1552 |         }
1553 |       }
1554 |     }
1555 | 
1556 |     return true;
1557 |   }

149 |     public MustDef apply(MustDef a, MustDef b) {
150 |       MustDef result = new MustDef();
151 |       Map<Var, Definition> resultMap = result.reachingDef;
152 | 
153 |       // Take the join of all variables that are not TOP in this.
154 |       for (Map.Entry<Var, Definition> varEntry : a.reachingDef.entrySet()) {
155 |         Var var = varEntry.getKey();
156 |         Definition aDef = varEntry.getValue();
157 | 
158 |         if (aDef == null) {
159 |           // "a" is BOTTOM implies that the variable has more than one possible
160 |           // definition. We set the join of this to be BOTTOM regardless of what
161 |           // "b" might be.
162 |           resultMap.put(var, null);
163 |           continue;
164 |         }
165 | 
166 |         Node aNode = aDef.node;
167 | 
168 |         if (b.reachingDef.containsKey(var)) {
169 |           Definition bDef = b.reachingDef.get(var);
170 | 
171 |           if (aDef.equals(bDef)) {
172 |             resultMap.put(var, aDef);
173 |           } else {
174 |             resultMap.put(var, null);
175 |           }
176 |         } else {
177 |           resultMap.put(var, aDef);
178 |         }
179 |       }

182 |       // in this.

85 |   void add(Node n, Context context) {
86 |     if (!cc.continueProcessing()) {
87 |       return;
88 |     }

91 |     String opstr = NodeUtil.opToStr(type);
92 |     int childCount = n.getChildCount();
93 |     Node first = n.getFirstChild();
94 |     Node last = n.getLastChild();
95 | 
96 |     // Handle all binary operators
97 |     if (opstr != null && first != last) {
98 |       Preconditions.checkState(
99 |           childCount == 2,
100 |           "Bad binary operator \"%s\": expected 2 arguments but got %s",
101 |           opstr, childCount);
102 |       int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
103 | 
104 |       // For right-hand-side of operations, only pass context if it's
105 |       // the IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE one.
106 |       Context rhsContext = getContextForNoInOperator(context);
107 | 
108 |       // Handle associativity.
109 |       // e.g. if the parse tree is a * (b * c),
110 |       // we can simply generate a * b * c.
111 |       if (last.getType() == type &&
112 |           NodeUtil.isAssociative(type)) {
113 |         addExpr(first, p, context);

115 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
116 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(last)) {
117 |         // Assignments are the only right-associative binary operators
118 |         addExpr(first, p, context);
119 |         cc.addOp(opstr, true);
120 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
121 |       } else {
122 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, type, opstr, context, rhsContext, p, p + 1);
123 |       }
124 |       return;
125 |     }
126 | 
127 |     cc.startSourceMapping(n);

129 |     switch (type) {

132 |                 !first.getNext().hasMoreThanOneChild());

141 |         if (catchblock != null) {
142 |           add(catchblock);
143 |         }

148 |         }
149 |         break;

720 |         }

729 |     }

731 |     cc.endSourceMapping(n);

===== M0643 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!n.isExprResult() && !n.isVar()) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (forVar.isName()
85 |           && n.isVar() && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // OK, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.isFor()
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some JavaScript parsers (such
101 |       // as the PlayStation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (n.isVar()) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ClosureCodingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ClosureCodingConvention.java
Original range: 94-153
Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>Understands several different inheritance patterns that occur in
   * Google code (various uses of {@code inherits} and {@code mixin}).
   */
Method code:
94 |   @Override
95 |   public SubclassRelationship getClassesDefinedByCall(Node callNode) {
96 |     SubclassRelationship relationship =
97 |         super.getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
98 |     if (relationship != null) return relationship;
99 | 
100 |     Node callName = callNode.getFirstChild();
101 |     SubclassType type = typeofClassDefiningName(callName);
102 |     if (type != null) {
103 |       Node subclass = null;
104 |       Node superclass = callNode.getLastChild();
105 | 
106 |       // There are six possible syntaxes for a class-defining method:
107 |       // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
108 |       // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
109 |       // goog$inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
110 |       // SubClass.mixin(SuperClass.prototype)
111 |       // goog.mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
112 |       // goog$mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
113 |       boolean isDeprecatedCall = callNode.getChildCount() == 2 &&
114 |           callName.isGetProp();
115 |       if (isDeprecatedCall) {
116 |         // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
117 |         subclass = callName.getFirstChild();
118 |       } else if (callNode.getChildCount() == 3) {
119 |         // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
120 |         subclass = callName.getNext();
121 |       } else {
122 |         return null;
123 |       }
124 | 
125 |       if (type == SubclassType.MIXIN) {
126 |         // Only consider mixins that mix two prototypes as related to
127 |         // inheritance.
128 |         if (!endsWithPrototype(superclass)) {
129 |           return null;
130 |         }
131 |         if (!isDeprecatedCall) {
132 |           if (!endsWithPrototype(subclass)) {
133 |             return null;
134 |           }
135 |           // Strip off the prototype from the name.
136 |           subclass = subclass.getFirstChild();
137 |         }
138 |         superclass = superclass.getFirstChild();
139 |       }
140 | 
141 |       // bail out if either of the side of the "inherits"
142 |       // isn't a real class name. This prevents us from
143 |       // doing something weird in cases like:
144 |       // goog.inherits(MySubClass, cond ? SuperClass1 : BaseClass2)
145 |       if (subclass != null &&
146 |           subclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName() &&
147 |           superclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName()) {
148 |         return new SubclassRelationship(type, subclass, superclass);
149 |       }
150 |     }
151 | 
152 |     return null;
153 |   }

===== M0704 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeArgumentsArray.tryReplaceArguments(Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeArgumentsArray.java
Original range: 177-289
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to optimize all the arguments array access in this scope by assigning
   * a name to each element.
   *
   * @param scope scope of the function
   * @return true if any modification has been done to the AST
   */
Method code:
177 |   private boolean tryReplaceArguments(Scope scope) {
178 | 
179 |     Node parametersList = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
180 |     Preconditions.checkState(parametersList.isParamList());
181 | 
182 |     // Keep track of rather this function modified the AST and needs to be
183 |     // reported back to the compiler later.
184 |     boolean changed = false;
185 | 
186 |     // Number of parameter that can be accessed without using the arguments
187 |     // array.
188 |     int numNamedParameter = parametersList.getChildCount();
189 | 
190 |     // We want to guess what the highest index that has been access from the
191 |     // arguments array. We will guess that it does not use anything index higher
192 |     // than the named parameter list first until we see other wise.
193 |     int highestIndex = numNamedParameter - 1;
194 | 
195 |     // Iterate through all the references to arguments array in the function to
196 |     // determine the real highestIndex.
197 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
198 | 
199 |       Node getElem = ref.getParent();
200 | 
201 |       // Bail on anything but argument[c] access where c is a constant.
202 |       // TODO(user): We might not need to bail out all the time, there might
203 |       // be more cases that we can cover.
204 |       if (!getElem.isGetElem()) {
205 |         return false;
206 |       }
207 | 
208 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
209 | 
210 |       // We have something like arguments[x] where x is not a constant. That
211 |       // means at least one of the access is not known.
212 |       if (!index.isNumber()) {
213 |         // TODO(user): Its possible not to give up just yet. The type
214 |         // inference did a 'semi value propagation'. If we know that string
215 |         // is never a subclass of the type of the index. We'd know that
216 |         // it is never 'callee'.
217 |         return false; // Give up.
218 |       }
219 | 
220 |       Node getElemParent = getElem.getParent();
221 |       // When we have argument[0](), replacing it with a() is semantically
222 |       // different if argument[0] is a function call that refers to 'this'
223 |       if (getElemParent.isCall() &&
224 |           getElemParent.getFirstChild() == getElem) {
225 |         // TODO(user): We can consider using .call() if aliasing that
226 |         // argument allows shorter alias for other arguments.
227 |         return false;
228 |       }
229 | 
230 |       // Replace the highest index if we see an access that has a higher index
231 |       // than all the one we saw before.
232 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
233 |       if (value > highestIndex) {
234 |         highestIndex = value;
235 |       }
236 |     }
237 | 
238 |     // Number of extra arguments we need.
239 |     // For example: function() { arguments[3] } access index 3 so
240 |     // it will need 4 extra named arguments to changed into:
241 |     // function(a,b,c,d) { d }.
242 |     int numExtraArgs = highestIndex - numNamedParameter + 1;
243 | 
244 |     // Temporary holds the new names as string for quick access later.
245 |     String[] argNames = new String[numExtraArgs];
246 | 
247 |     // Insert the formal parameter to the method's signature.
248 |     // Example: function() --> function(r0, r1, r2)
249 |     for (int i = 0; i < numExtraArgs; i++) {
250 |       String name = getNewName();
251 |       argNames[i] = name;
252 |       parametersList.addChildrenToBack(IR.name(name));
253 |       changed = true;
254 |     }
255 | 
256 |     // This loop performs the replacement of arguments[x] -> a if x is known.
257 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
258 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
259 | 
260 |       // Skip if it is unknown.
261 |       if (!index.isNumber()) {
262 |         continue;
263 |       }
264 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
265 | 
266 |       // Unnamed parameter.
267 |       if (value >= numNamedParameter) {
268 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
269 |             IR.name(argNames[value - numNamedParameter]));
270 |       } else {
271 | 
272 |         // Here, for no apparent reason, the user is accessing a named parameter
273 |         // with arguments[idx]. We can replace it with the actual name for them.
274 |         Node name = parametersList.getFirstChild();
275 | 
276 |         // This is a linear search for the actual name from the signature.
277 |         // It is not necessary to make this fast because chances are the user
278 |         // will not deliberately write code like this.
279 |         for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) {
280 |           name = name.getNext();
281 |         }
282 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
283 |             IR.name(name.getString()));
284 |       }
285 |       changed = true;
286 |     }
287 | 
288 |     return changed;
289 |   }

===== M0734 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.assignNames(Set<Assignment>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 441-511
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
441 |   private void assignNames(Set<Assignment> varsToRename) {
442 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
443 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
444 | 
445 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
446 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator =
447 |         prefix.isEmpty() ? globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(
448 |             reservedNames, "", reservedCharacters);
449 | 
450 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
451 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
452 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
453 | 
454 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
455 |       if (a.newName != null) {
456 |         continue;
457 |       }
458 | 
459 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
460 |         continue;
461 |       }
462 | 
463 |       String newName;
464 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
465 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
466 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
467 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
468 |       } else {
469 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
470 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
471 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
472 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
473 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
474 |       }
475 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
476 |     }
477 | 
478 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
479 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
480 |     // follows:
481 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
482 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
483 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
484 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
485 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
486 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
487 |     //    compressible.
488 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
489 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
490 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
491 | 
492 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
493 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
494 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
495 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
496 | 
497 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
498 |       // generated names of the same length.
499 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
500 |       for (int j = i; j < numPendingAssignments
501 |           && generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len; j++) {
502 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
503 |       }
504 | 
505 |       // Now, make the assignments
506 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
507 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
508 |         ++i;
509 |       }
510 |     }
511 |   }

Method code:
639 |   private void handleReturn(Node node) {
640 |     Node lastJump = null;
641 |     for (Iterator<Node> iter = exceptionHandler.iterator(); iter.hasNext();) {
642 |       Node curHandler = iter.next();
643 |       if (curHandler.isFunction()) {
644 |         break;
645 |       }
646 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(curHandler)) {
647 |         if (lastJump == null) {
648 |           createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, curHandler.getLastChild());
649 |         } else {
650 |           finallyMap.put(lastJump,
651 |               computeFallThrough(curHandler.getLastChild()));
652 |         }
653 |         lastJump = curHandler;
654 |       }
655 |     }
656 | 
657 |     if (node.hasChildren()) {
658 |       connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(node, node.getFirstChild());
659 |     }
660 | 
661 |     if (lastJump == null) {
662 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, null);
663 |     } else {
664 |       finallyMap.put(lastJump, null);
665 |     }
666 |   }

===== M0769 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.JSModuleGraph.manageDependencies(DependencyOptions,List<CompilerInput>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/JSModuleGraph.java
Original range: 311-390
Documentation:
/**
   * Apply the dependency options to the list of sources, returning a new
   * source list re-ordering and dropping files as necessary.
   * This module graph will be updated to reflect the new list.
   *
   * @param inputs The original list of sources. Used to ensure that the sort
   *     is stable.
   * @throws CircularDependencyException if there is a circular dependency
   *     between the provides and requires.
   * @throws MissingProvideException if an entry point was not provided
   *     by any of the inputs.
   * @see DependencyOptions for more info on how this works.
   */
Method code:
311 |   public List<CompilerInput> manageDependencies(
312 |       DependencyOptions depOptions,
313 |       List<CompilerInput> inputs)
314 |       throws CircularDependencyException, MissingProvideException {
315 | 
316 |     SortedDependencies<CompilerInput> sorter =
317 |         new SortedDependencies<CompilerInput>(inputs);
318 |     Set<CompilerInput> entryPointInputs = Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
319 |     if (depOptions.shouldPruneDependencies()) {
320 |       if (!depOptions.shouldDropMoochers()) {
321 |         entryPointInputs.addAll(sorter.getInputsWithoutProvides());
322 |       }
323 | 
324 |       for (String entryPoint : depOptions.getEntryPoints()) {
325 |         entryPointInputs.add(sorter.getInputProviding(entryPoint));
326 |       }
327 | 
328 |       CompilerInput baseJs = sorter.maybeGetInputProviding("goog");
329 |       if (baseJs != null) {
330 |         entryPointInputs.add(baseJs);
331 |       }
332 |     } else {
333 |       entryPointInputs.addAll(inputs);
334 |     }
335 | 
336 |     // The order of inputs, sorted independently of modules.
337 |     List<CompilerInput> absoluteOrder =
338 |         sorter.getDependenciesOf(inputs, depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
339 | 
340 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module.
341 |     ListMultimap<JSModule, CompilerInput> entryPointInputsPerModule =
342 |         LinkedListMultimap.create();
343 |     for (CompilerInput input : entryPointInputs) {
344 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
345 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(module);
346 |       entryPointInputsPerModule.put(module, input);
347 |     }
348 | 
349 |     // Clear the modules of their inputs. This also nulls out
350 |     // the input's reference to its module.
351 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
352 |       module.removeAll();
353 |     }
354 | 
355 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module, or in one
356 |     // of that module's dependencies.
357 |     for (JSModule module : entryPointInputsPerModule.keySet()) {
358 |       List<CompilerInput> transitiveClosure =
359 |           sorter.getDependenciesOf(
360 |               entryPointInputsPerModule.get(module),
361 |               depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
362 |       for (CompilerInput input : transitiveClosure) {
363 |         JSModule oldModule = input.getModule();
364 |         if (oldModule == null) {
365 |           input.setModule(module);
366 |         } else {
367 |           input.setModule(null);
368 |           input.setModule(
369 |               getDeepestCommonDependencyInclusive(oldModule, module));
370 |         }
371 |       }
372 |     }
373 | 
374 |     // All the inputs are pointing to the modules that own them. Yeah!
375 |     // Update the modules to reflect this.
376 |     for (CompilerInput input : absoluteOrder) {
377 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
378 |       if (module != null) {
379 |         module.add(input);
380 |       }
381 |     }
382 | 
383 |     // Now, generate the sorted result.
384 |     List<CompilerInput> result = Lists.newArrayList();
385 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
386 |       result.addAll(module.getInputs());
387 |     }
388 | 
389 |     return result;
390 |   }

   * Generates the next short name.

119 |   String generateNextName() {

121 |       String name = prefix;
122 |

124 | 
125 |       if (name.isEmpty()) {

===== M0787 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ExploitAssigns.isCollapsibleValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ExploitAssigns.java
Original range: 76-91
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines whether we know enough about the given value to be able
   * to collapse it into subsequent expressions.
   *
   * For example, we can collapse booleans and variable names:
   * <code>
   * x = 3; y = x; // y = x = 3;
   * a = true; b = true; // b = a = true;
   * <code>
   * But we won't try to collapse complex expressions.
   *
   * @param value The value node.
   * @param isLValue Whether it's on the left-hand side of an expr.
   */
Method code:
76 |   private boolean isCollapsibleValue(Node value, boolean isLValue) {
77 |     switch (value.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.GETPROP:
79 |         // Do not collapse GETPROPs on arbitrary objects, because
80 |         // they may be implemented setter functions, and oftentimes
81 |         // setter functions fail on native objects. This is OK for "THIS"
82 |         // objects, because we assume that they are non-native.
83 |         return !isLValue || value.getFirstChild().isThis();
84 | 
85 |       case Token.NAME:
86 |         return true;
87 | 
88 |       default:
89 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value);
90 |     }
91 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.moveNamedFunctions(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 640-672
Documentation:
/**
     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
     * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.
     */
Method code:
640 |     private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {
641 |       Preconditions.checkState(
642 |           functionBody.getParent().isFunction());
643 |       Node previous = null;
644 |       Node current = functionBody.getFirstChild();
645 |       // Skip any declarations at the beginning of the function body, they
646 |       // are already in the right place.
647 |       while (current != null && NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
648 |         previous = current;
649 |         current = current.getNext();
650 |       }
651 | 
652 |       // Find any remaining declarations and move them.
653 |       Node insertAfter = previous;
654 |       while (current != null) {
655 |         // Save off the next node as the current node maybe removed.
656 |         Node next = current.getNext();
657 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
658 |           // Remove the declaration from the body.
659 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(previous);
660 |           functionBody.removeChildAfter(previous);
661 | 
662 |           // Read the function at the top of the function body (after any
663 |           // previous declarations).
664 |           insertAfter = addToFront(functionBody, current, insertAfter);
665 |           reportCodeChange("Move function declaration not at top of function");
666 |         } else {
667 |           // Update the previous only if the current node hasn't been moved.
668 |           previous = current;
669 |         }
670 |         current = next;
671 |       }
672 |     }

===== M0804 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 513-535
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An r-value in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
513 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
514 |       switch (n.getType()) {
515 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
516 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
517 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
518 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
519 |         case Token.OR:
520 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
521 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
522 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
523 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
524 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
525 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
526 |         case Token.HOOK:
527 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
528 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
529 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
530 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
531 |           Node third = second.getNext();
532 |           return getValueType(third);
533 |       }
534 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
535 |     }

138 |     // Process the body of the function.
139 |     Preconditions.checkState(t.getScopeRoot().isFunction());
140 |     cfa.process(null, t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild());
141 |     cfg = cfa.getCfg();
142 |     reachingDef = new MustBeReachingVariableDef(cfg, t.getScope(), compiler);
143 |     reachingDef.analyze();
144 |     candidates = Lists.newLinkedList();
145 | 
146 |     // Using the forward reaching definition search to find all the inline
147 |     // candidates
148 |     new NodeTraversal(compiler, new GatherCandiates()).traverse(
149 |         t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild());
150 | 
151 |     // Compute the backward reaching use. The CFG can be reused.
152 |     reachingUses = new MaybeReachingVariableUse(cfg, t.getScope(), compiler);
153 |     reachingUses.analyze();
154 |     for (Candidate c : candidates) {
155 |       if (c.canInline()) {
156 |         c.inlineVariable();
157 | 
158 |         // If definition c has dependencies, then inlining it may have
159 |         // introduced new dependencies for our other inlining candidates.
160 |         //
161 |         // MustBeReachingVariableDef uses this dependency graph in its
162 |         // analysis, so some of these candidates may no longer be valid.
163 |         // We keep track of when the variable dependency graph changed
164 |         // so that we can back off appropriately.
165 |         if (!c.defMetadata.depends.isEmpty()) {
166 |           inlinedNewDependencies.add(t.getScope().getVar(c.varName));
167 |         }
168 |       }
169 |     }
170 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.computeGenKill(Node,BitSet,BitSet,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 184-275
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the GEN and KILL set.
   *
   * @param n Root node.
   * @param gen Local variables that are live because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param kill Local variables that are killed because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param conditional {@code true} if any assignments encountered are
   *        conditionally executed. These assignments might not kill a variable.
   */
Method code:
184 |   private void computeGenKill(Node n, BitSet gen, BitSet kill,
185 |       boolean conditional) {
186 | 
187 |     switch (n.getType()) {
188 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
189 |       case Token.BLOCK:
190 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
191 |         return;
192 | 
193 |       case Token.WHILE:
194 |       case Token.DO:
195 |       case Token.IF:
196 |         computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
197 |             conditional);
198 |         return;
199 | 
200 |       case Token.FOR:
201 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
202 |           computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
203 |               conditional);
204 |         } else {
205 |           // for(x in y) {...}
206 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
207 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
208 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
209 |             // for(var x in y) {...}
210 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild();
211 |           }
212 | 
213 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
214 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
215 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
216 |           } else {
217 |             computeGenKill(lhs, gen, kill, conditional);
218 |           }
219 | 
220 |           // rhs is executed only once so we don't go into it every loop.
221 |         }
222 |         return;
223 | 
224 |       case Token.VAR:
225 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
226 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
227 |             computeGenKill(c.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
228 |             if (!conditional) {
229 |               addToSetIfLocal(c, kill);
230 |             }
231 |           }
232 |         }
233 |         return;
234 | 
235 |       case Token.AND:
236 |       case Token.OR:
237 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
238 |         // May short circuit.
239 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
240 |         return;
241 | 
242 |       case Token.HOOK:
243 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
244 |         // Assume both sides are conditional.
245 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), gen, kill, true);
246 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
247 |         return;
248 | 
249 |       case Token.NAME:
250 |         if (isArgumentsName(n)) {
251 |           markAllParametersEscaped();
252 |         } else {
253 |           addToSetIfLocal(n, gen);
254 |         }
255 |         return;
256 | 
257 |       default:
258 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
259 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
260 |           if (!conditional) {
261 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
262 |           }
263 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
264 |             // assignments such as a += 1 reads a.
265 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
266 |           }
267 |           computeGenKill(lhs.getNext(), gen, kill, conditional);
268 |         } else {
269 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
270 |             computeGenKill(c, gen, kill, conditional);
271 |           }
272 |         }
273 |         return;
274 |     }
275 |   }

/**
   * Try to fold an array join: ['a', 'b', 'c'].join('') -> 'abc';
   */
Method code:
393 |   private Node tryFoldArrayJoin(Node n) {
394 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
395 | 
396 |     if (callTarget == null || !callTarget.isGetProp()) {
397 |       return n;
398 |     }
399 | 
400 |     Node right = callTarget.getNext();
401 |     if (right != null) {
402 |       if (right.getNext() != null || !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(right)) {
403 |         return n;
404 |       }
405 |     }
406 | 
407 |     Node arrayNode = callTarget.getFirstChild();
408 |     Node functionName = arrayNode.getNext();
409 | 
410 |     if (!arrayNode.isArrayLit() ||
411 |         !functionName.getString().equals("join")) {
412 |       return n;
413 |     }
414 | 
415 |     if (right != null && right.isString()
416 |         && ",".equals(right.getString())) {
417 |       // "," is the default, it doesn't need to be explicit
418 |       n.removeChild(right);
419 |       reportCodeChange();
420 |     }
421 | 
422 |     String joinString = (right == null) ? "," : NodeUtil.getStringValue(right);
423 |     List<Node> arrayFoldedChildren = Lists.newLinkedList();
424 |     StringBuilder sb = null;
425 |     int foldedSize = 0;
426 |     Node prev = null;
427 |     Node elem = arrayNode.getFirstChild();
428 |     // Merges adjacent String nodes.
429 |     while (elem != null) {
430 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(elem) || elem.isEmpty()) {
431 |         if (sb == null) {
432 |           sb = new StringBuilder();
433 |         } else {
434 |           sb.append(joinString);
435 |         }
436 |         sb.append(NodeUtil.getArrayElementStringValue(elem));
437 |       } else {
438 |         if (sb != null) {
439 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
440 |           // + 2 for the quotes.
441 |           foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
442 |           arrayFoldedChildren.add(
443 |               IR.string(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
444 |           sb = null;
445 |         }
446 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(elem);
447 |         arrayFoldedChildren.add(elem);
448 |       }
449 |       prev = elem;
450 |       elem = elem.getNext();
451 |     }
452 | 
453 |     if (sb != null) {
454 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
455 |       // + 2 for the quotes.
456 |       foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
457 |       arrayFoldedChildren.add(
458 |           IR.string(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
459 |     }
460 |     // one for each comma.
461 |     foldedSize += arrayFoldedChildren.size() - 1;
462 | 
463 |     int originalSize = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(n);
464 |     switch (arrayFoldedChildren.size()) {
465 |       case 0:
466 |         Node emptyStringNode = IR.string("");
467 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, emptyStringNode);
468 |         reportCodeChange();
469 |         return emptyStringNode;
470 |       case 1:
471 |         Node foldedStringNode = arrayFoldedChildren.remove(0);
472 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
473 |           return n;
474 |         }
475 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
476 |         if (!foldedStringNode.isString()) {
477 |           // If the Node is not a string literal, ensure that
478 |           // it is coerced to a string.
479 |           Node replacement = IR.add(
480 |               IR.string("").srcref(n),
481 |               foldedStringNode);
482 |           foldedStringNode = replacement;
483 |         }
484 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, foldedStringNode);
485 |         reportCodeChange();
486 |         return foldedStringNode;
487 |       default:
488 |         // No folding could actually be performed.
489 |         if (arrayFoldedChildren.size() == arrayNode.getChildCount()) {
490 |           return n;
491 |         }
492 |         int kJoinOverhead = "[].join()".length();
493 |         foldedSize += kJoinOverhead;
494 |         foldedSize += (right != null) ? InlineCostEstimator.getCost(right) : 0;
495 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
496 |           return n;
497 |         }
498 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
499 |         for (Node node : arrayFoldedChildren) {
500 |           arrayNode.addChildToBack(node);
501 |         }
502 |         reportCodeChange();
503 |         break;
504 |     }
505 | 
506 |     return n;
507 |   }

46 |   private static boolean canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
47 |     // Fold only statement block. NOT scripts block.
48 |     if (!block.isBlock()) {
49 |       return false;
50 |     }
51 |

55 |     }

===== M0884 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineObjectLiterals.InliningBehavior.isInlinableObject(List<Reference>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineObjectLiterals.java
Original range: 155-250
Documentation:
/**
     * Counts the number of direct (full) references to an object.
     * Specifically, we check for references of the following type:
     * <pre>
     *   x;
     *   x.fn();
     * </pre>
     */
Method code:
155 |     private boolean isInlinableObject(List<Reference> refs) {
156 |       boolean ret = false;
157 |       Set<String> validProperties = Sets.newHashSet();
158 |       for (Reference ref : refs) {
159 |         Node name = ref.getNode();
160 |         Node parent = ref.getParent();
161 |         Node gramps = ref.getGrandparent();
162 | 
163 |         // Ignore indirect references, like x.y (except x.y(), since
164 |         // the function referenced by y might reference 'this').
165 |         //
166 |         if (parent.isGetProp()) {
167 |           Preconditions.checkState(parent.getFirstChild() == name);
168 |           // A call target maybe using the object as a 'this' value.
169 |           if (gramps.isCall()
170 |               && gramps.getFirstChild() == parent) {
171 |             return false;
172 |           }
173 | 
174 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): This pass's object-splitting algorithm has
175 |           // a blind spot. It assumes that if a property isn't defined on an
176 |           // object, then the value is undefined. This is not true, because
177 |           // Object.prototype can have arbitrary properties on it.
178 |           //
179 |           // We short-circuit this problem by bailing out if we see a reference
180 |           // to a property that isn't defined on the object literal. This
181 |           // isn't a perfect algorithm, but it should catch most cases.
182 |           String propName = parent.getLastChild().getString();
183 |           if (!validProperties.contains(propName)) {
184 |             if (NodeUtil.isVarOrSimpleAssignLhs(parent, gramps)) {
185 |               validProperties.add(propName);
186 |             } else {
187 |               return false;
188 |             }
189 |           }
190 |           continue;
191 |         }
192 | 
193 |         // Only rewrite VAR declarations or simple assignment statements
194 |         if (!isVarOrAssignExprLhs(name)) {
195 |            return false;
196 |         }
197 | 
198 |         Node val = ref.getAssignedValue();
199 |         if (val == null) {
200 |           // A var with no assignment.
201 |           continue;
202 |         }
203 | 
204 |         // We're looking for object literal assignments only.
205 |         if (!val.isObjectLit()) {
206 |           return false;
207 |         }
208 | 
209 |         // Make sure that the value is not self-referential. IOW,
210 |         // disallow things like x = {b: x.a}.
211 |         //
212 |         // TODO: Only exclude unorderable self-referential
213 |         // assignments. i.e. x = {a: x.b, b: x.a} is not orderable,
214 |         // but x = {a: 1, b: x.a} is.
215 |         //
216 |         // Also, ES5 getters/setters aren't handled by this pass.
217 |         for (Node child = val.getFirstChild(); child != null;
218 |              child = child.getNext()) {
219 |           if (child.isGetterDef() ||
220 |               child.isSetterDef()) {
221 |             // ES5 get/set not supported.
222 |             return false;
223 |           }
224 | 
225 |           validProperties.add(child.getString());
226 | 
227 |           Node childVal = child.getFirstChild();
228 |           // Check if childVal is the parent of any of the passed in
229 |           // references, as that is how self-referential assignments
230 |           // will happen.
231 |           for (Reference t : refs) {
232 |             Node refNode = t.getParent();
233 |             while (!NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(refNode)) {
234 |               if (refNode == childVal) {
235 |                 // There's a self-referential assignment
236 |                 return false;
237 |               }
238 |               refNode = refNode.getParent();
239 |             }
240 |           }
241 |         }
242 | 
243 | 
244 |         // We have found an acceptable object literal assignment. As
245 |         // long as there are no other assignments that mess things up,
246 |         // we can inline.
247 |         ret = true;
248 |       }
249 |       return ret;
250 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(Node,Node,Node,int,String)

Original range: 220-271
Documentation:
/**
   * Look for exits (returns, breaks, or continues, depending on the context) at
   * the end of a block and removes them by moving the if node's siblings,
   * if any, into the opposite condition block.
   *
   * @param srcBlock The block to inspect.
   * @param destBlock The block to move sibling nodes into.
   * @param ifNode The if node to work with.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName The name associated with the exit, if any.
   * @nullable labelName null for anything excepted for named-break associated
   *           with a label.
   */
Method code:
220 |   private void tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(Node srcBlock, Node destBlock,
221 |       Node ifNode, int exitType, String labelName) {
222 |     Node exitNodeParent = null;
223 |     Node exitNode = null;
224 | 
225 |     // Pick an exit node candidate.
226 |     if (srcBlock.isBlock()) {
227 |       if (!srcBlock.hasChildren()) {
228 |         return;
229 |       }
230 |       exitNodeParent = srcBlock;
231 |       exitNode = exitNodeParent.getLastChild();
232 |     } else {
233 |       // Just a single statement, if it isn't an exit bail.
234 |       exitNodeParent = ifNode;
235 |       exitNode = srcBlock;
236 |     }
237 | 
238 |     // Verify the candidate.
239 |     if (!matchingExitNode(exitNode, exitType, labelName)) {
240 |       return;
241 |     }
242 | 
243 |     // Take case of the if nodes siblings, if any.
244 |     if (ifNode.getNext() != null) {
245 |       // Move siblings of the if block into the opposite
246 |       // logic block of the exit.
247 |       Node newDestBlock = IR.block().srcref(ifNode);
248 |       if (destBlock == null) {
249 |         // Only possible if this is the false block.
250 |         ifNode.addChildToBack(newDestBlock);
251 |       } else if (destBlock.isEmpty()) {
252 |         // Use the new block.
253 |         ifNode.replaceChild(destBlock, newDestBlock);
254 |       } else if (destBlock.isBlock()) {
255 |         // Reuse the existing block.
256 |         newDestBlock = destBlock;
257 |       } else {
258 |         // Add the existing statement to the new block.
259 |         ifNode.replaceChild(destBlock, newDestBlock);
260 |         newDestBlock.addChildToBack(destBlock);
261 |       }
262 | 
263 |       // Move all the if node's following siblings.
264 |       moveAllFollowing(ifNode, ifNode.getParent(), newDestBlock);
265 |     }
266 | 
267 |     // Get rid of the "exit", replace with an empty item if needed.
268 |     NodeUtil.removeChild(exitNodeParent, exitNode);
269 | 
270 |     compiler.reportCodeChange();
271 |   }

===== M0917 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.UnreachableCodeElimination.tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/UnreachableCodeElimination.java
Original range: 130-179
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to remove n if an unconditional branch node (break, continue or
   * return) if the target of n is the same as the the follow of n. That is, if
   * we remove n, the control flow remains the same. Also if n targets to
   * another unconditional branch, this function will recursively try to remove
   * the target branch as well. The reason why we want to cascade this removal
   * is because we only run this pass once. If we have code such as
   *
   * break -> break -> break
   *
   * where all 3 break's are useless. The order of removal matters. When we
   * first look at the first break, we see that it branches to the 2nd break.
   * However, if we remove the last break, the 2nd break becomes useless and
   * finally the first break becomes useless as well.
   *
   * @return The target of this jump. If the target is also useless jump,
   *     the target of that useless jump recursively.
   */
Method code:
130 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
131 |   private Node tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node n) {
132 |     /*
133 |      * For each of the unconditional branching control flow node, check to see
134 |      * if the ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode of that node is same as
135 |      * the branching target. If it is, the branch node is safe to be removed.
136 |      *
137 |      * This is not as clever as MinimizeExitPoints because it doesn't do any
138 |      * if-else conversion but it handles more complicated switch statements
139 |      * much nicer.
140 |      */
141 | 
142 |     // If n is null the target is the end of the function, nothing to do.
143 |     if (n == null) {
144 |        return n;
145 |     }
146 | 
147 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = curCfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
148 | 
149 |     if (gNode == null) {
150 |       return n;
151 |     }
152 | 
153 |     switch (n.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.RETURN:
155 |         if (n.hasChildren()) {
156 |           break;
157 |         }
158 |       case Token.BREAK:
159 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
160 | 
161 |         // We are looking for a control flow changing statement that always
162 |         // branches to the same node. If removing it the control flow still
163 |         // branches to that same node. It is safe to remove it.
164 |         List<DiGraphEdge<Node,Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
165 |         if (outEdges.size() == 1 &&
166 |             // If there is a next node, there is no chance this jump is useless.
167 |             (n.getNext() == null || n.getNext().isFunction())) {
168 | 
169 |           Preconditions.checkState(outEdges.get(0).getValue() == Branch.UNCOND);
170 |           Node fallThrough = computeFollowing(n);
171 |           Node nextCfgNode = outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue();
172 |           if (nextCfgNode == fallThrough) {
173 |             removeDeadExprStatementSafely(n);
174 |             return fallThrough;
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 |     }
178 |     return n;
179 |   }

===== M0921 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 692-789
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
692 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
693 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
694 |     /*
695 |      * This is the case where:
696 |      *
697 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
698 |      * the script.
699 |      *
700 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
701 |      * the caller of the function.
702 |      *
703 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
704 |      * back to the caller of the function.
705 |      *
706 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
707 |      * asked to traverse.
708 |      *
709 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
710 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
711 |      */
712 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
713 |     if (parent == null || parent.isFunction() ||
714 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
715 |       return null;
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
719 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
720 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
721 |       case Token.IF:
722 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
723 |       case Token.CASE:
724 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
725 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
726 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
727 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
728 |           if (parent.getNext().isCase()) {
729 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
730 |           } else if (parent.getNext().isDefaultCase()) {
731 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
732 |           } else {
733 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
734 |           }
735 |         } else {
736 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
737 |         }
738 |         break;
739 |       case Token.FOR:
740 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
741 |           return parent;
742 |         } else {
743 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
744 |         }
745 |       case Token.WHILE:
746 |       case Token.DO:
747 |         return parent;
748 |       case Token.TRY:
749 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
750 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
751 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
752 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
753 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
754 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
755 |           }
756 |         // CATCH block.
757 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
758 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
759 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
760 |           } else {
761 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
762 |           }
763 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
764 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
765 |           if (cfa != null) {
766 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
767 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.ON_EX, finallyNode);
768 |             }
769 |           }
770 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
771 |         }
772 |     }
773 | 
774 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
775 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
776 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
777 | 
778 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
779 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.isFunction()) {
780 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
781 |     }
782 | 
783 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
784 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
785 |     } else {
786 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transferred up the AST.
787 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
788 |     }
789 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 3110-3149
Documentation:
/**
   * @returns false iff the result of the expression is not consumed.
   */
Method code:
3110 |   static boolean isExpressionResultUsed(Node expr) {
3111 |     // TODO(johnlenz): consider sharing some code with trySimpleUnusedResult.
3112 |     Node parent = expr.getParent();
3113 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
3114 |       case Token.BLOCK:
3115 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
3116 |         return false;
3117 |       case Token.HOOK:
3118 |       case Token.AND:
3119 |       case Token.OR:
3120 |         return (expr == parent.getFirstChild())
3121 |             ? true : isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3122 |       case Token.COMMA:
3123 |         Node gramps = parent.getParent();
3124 |         if (gramps.isCall() &&
3125 |             parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
3126 |           // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
3127 |           // call to an eval. See ECMA-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's OK for the first
3128 |           // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
3129 |           // an eval. This we pretend that this is "used".
3130 |           if (expr == parent.getFirstChild() &&
3131 |               parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
3132 |               expr.getNext().isName() &&
3133 |               "eval".equals(expr.getNext().getString())) {
3134 |             return true;
3135 |           }
3136 |         }
3137 | 
3138 |         return (expr == parent.getFirstChild())
3139 |             ? false : isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3140 |       case Token.FOR:
3141 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
3142 |           // Only an expression whose result is in the condition part of the
3143 |           // expression is used.
3144 |           return (parent.getChildAtIndex(1) == expr);
3145 |         }
3146 |         break;
3147 |     }
3148 |     return true;
3149 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.SortedDependencies.SortedDependencies(List<INPUT>)

Method code:
64 |   public SortedDependencies(List<INPUT> inputs)
65 |       throws CircularDependencyException {
66 |     this.inputs = Lists.newArrayList(inputs);
67 |     noProvides = Lists.newArrayList();
68 | 
69 |     // Collect all symbols provided in these files.
70 |     for (INPUT input : inputs) {
71 |       Collection<String> currentProvides = input.getProvides();
72 |       if (currentProvides.isEmpty()) {
73 |         noProvides.add(input);
74 |       }
75 | 
76 |       for (String provide : currentProvides) {
77 |         provideMap.put(provide, input);
78 |       }
79 |     }
80 | 
81 |     // Get the direct dependencies.
82 |     final Multimap<INPUT, INPUT> deps = HashMultimap.create();
83 |     for (INPUT input : inputs) {
84 |       for (String req : input.getRequires()) {
85 |         INPUT dep = provideMap.get(req);
86 |         if (dep != null && dep != input) {
87 |           deps.put(input, dep);
88 |         }
89 |       }
90 |     }
91 | 
92 |     // Sort the inputs by sucking in 0-in-degree nodes until we're done.
93 |     sortedList = topologicalStableSort(inputs, deps);
94 | 
95 |     // The dependency graph of inputs has a cycle iff sortedList is a proper
96 |     // subset of inputs. Also, it has a cycle iff the subgraph
97 |     // (inputs - sortedList) has a cycle. It's fairly easy to prove this
98 |     // by the lemma that a graph has a cycle iff it has a subgraph where
99 |     // no nodes have out-degree 0. I'll leave the proof of this as an exercise
100 |     // to the reader.
101 |     if (sortedList.size() < inputs.size()) {
102 |       List<INPUT> subGraph = Lists.newArrayList(inputs);
103 |       subGraph.removeAll(sortedList);
104 | 
105 |       throw new CircularDependencyException(
106 |           cycleToString(findCycle(subGraph, deps)));
107 |     }
108 |   }

===== M0960 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 148-190
Documentation:

Method code:
148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.isFunction()) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

/**
   * Determines if n matches the type and name for the following types of
   * "exits":
   *    - return without values
   *    - continues and breaks with or without names.
   * @param n The node to inspect.
   * @param type The Token type to look for.

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 560-607
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
560 |     private void extractForInitializer(
561 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
562 | 
563 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
564 |         next = c.getNext();
565 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
566 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
567 |         switch (c.getType()) {
568 |           case Token.LABEL:
569 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
570 |             break;
571 |           case Token.FOR:
572 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
573 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
574 |               if (first.isVar()) {
575 |                 // Transform:
576 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
577 |                 // to:
578 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
579 |                 Node newStatement = first;
580 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
581 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
582 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
583 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
584 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
585 |               }
586 |             } else if (!c.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
587 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
588 |               Node empty = IR.empty();
589 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
590 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
591 | 
592 |               Node newStatement;
593 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
594 |               // but are handled differently.
595 |               if (init.isVar()) {
596 |                 newStatement = init;
597 |               } else {
598 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
599 |               }
600 | 
601 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
602 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
603 |             }
604 |             break;
605 |         }
606 |       }
607 |     }

===== M0984 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 790-934
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
790 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
791 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
792 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
793 |     // that we know to be safe
794 |     switch (n.getType()) {
795 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
796 |       case Token.AND:
797 |       case Token.BLOCK:
798 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
799 |       case Token.HOOK:
800 |       case Token.IF:
801 |       case Token.IN:
802 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
803 |       case Token.NUMBER:
804 |       case Token.OR:
805 |       case Token.THIS:
806 |       case Token.TRUE:
807 |       case Token.FALSE:
808 |       case Token.NULL:
809 |       case Token.STRING:
810 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
811 |       case Token.SWITCH:
812 |       case Token.TRY:
813 |       case Token.EMPTY:
814 |         break;
815 | 
816 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
817 |       case Token.THROW:
818 |         return true;
819 | 
820 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
821 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
822 |           return true;
823 |         }
824 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
825 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
826 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
827 |             return true;
828 |           }
829 |         }
830 |         return false;
831 | 
832 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
833 |       case Token.REGEXP:
834 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
835 |           return true;
836 |         }
837 |         break;
838 | 
839 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
840 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
841 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
842 |           return true;
843 |         }
844 |         break;
845 | 
846 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
847 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
848 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
849 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
850 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
851 | 
852 |       case Token.NEW:
853 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
854 |           return true;
855 |         }
856 | 
857 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
858 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
859 |           // side-effects
860 |           break;
861 |         }
862 |         return true;
863 | 
864 |       case Token.CALL:
865 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
866 |         // side effect property set.
867 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
868 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
869 |           // side-effects
870 |           break;
871 |         }
872 |         return true;
873 | 
874 |       default:
875 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType())) {
876 |           break;
877 |         }
878 | 
879 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
880 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
881 |           if (assignTarget.isName()) {
882 |             return true;
883 |           }
884 | 
885 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
886 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
887 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
888 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
889 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
890 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
891 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
892 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
893 |             return true;
894 |           }
895 | 
896 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
897 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
898 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
899 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
900 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
901 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
902 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
903 |               return false;
904 |             }
905 | 
906 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
907 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
908 |             // other objects.
909 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
910 |             // side-effect.
911 |             while (isGet(current)) {
912 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
913 |             }
914 | 
915 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
916 |           } else {
917 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
918 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
919 |             // preserve existing behavior.
920 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
921 |           }
922 |         }
923 | 
924 |         return true;
925 |     }
926 | 
927 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
928 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
929 |         return true;
930 |       }
931 |     }
932 | 
933 |     return false;
934 |   }

===== M0987 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.tryMinimizeExits(Node,int,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MinimizeExitPoints.java
Original range: 114-205
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempts to minimize the number of explicit exit points in a control
   * structure to take advantage of the implied exit at the end of the
   * structure.  This is accomplished by removing redundant statements, and
   * moving statements following a qualifying IF node into that node.
   * For example:
   *
   * function () {
   *   if (x) return;
   *   else blah();
   *   foo();
   * }
   *
   * becomes:
   *
   * function () {
   *  if (x) ;
   *  else {
   *    blah();
   *    foo();
   *  }
   *
   * @param n The execution node of a parent to inspect.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName If parent is a label the name of the label to look for,
   *   null otherwise.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks within labels.
   */
Method code:
114 |   void tryMinimizeExits(Node n, int exitType, String labelName) {
115 | 
116 |     // Just an 'exit'.
117 |     if (matchingExitNode(n, exitType, labelName)) {
118 |       NodeUtil.removeChild(n.getParent(), n);
119 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
120 |       return;
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     // Just an 'if'.
124 |     if (n.isIf()) {
125 |       Node ifBlock = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
126 |       tryMinimizeExits(ifBlock, exitType, labelName);
127 |       Node elseBlock = ifBlock.getNext();
128 |       if (elseBlock != null) {
129 |         tryMinimizeExits(elseBlock, exitType, labelName);
130 |       }
131 |       return;
132 |     }
133 | 
134 |     // Just a 'try/catch/finally'.
135 |     if (n.isTry()) {
136 |       Node tryBlock = n.getFirstChild();
137 |       tryMinimizeExits(tryBlock, exitType, labelName);
138 |       Node allCatchNodes = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(n);
139 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(allCatchNodes)) {
140 |         Preconditions.checkState(allCatchNodes.hasOneChild());
141 |         Node catchNode = allCatchNodes.getFirstChild();
142 |         Node catchCodeBlock = catchNode.getLastChild();
143 |         tryMinimizeExits(catchCodeBlock, exitType, labelName);
144 |       }
145 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(n)) {
146 |         Node finallyBlock = n.getLastChild();
147 |         tryMinimizeExits(finallyBlock, exitType, labelName);
148 |       }
149 |     }
150 | 
151 |     // Just a 'label'.
152 |     if (n.isLabel()) {
153 |       Node labelBlock = n.getLastChild();
154 |       tryMinimizeExits(labelBlock, exitType, labelName);
155 |     }
156 | 
157 |     // TODO(johnlenz): The last case of SWITCH statement?
158 | 
159 |     // The rest assumes a block with at least one child, bail on anything else.
160 |     if (!n.isBlock() || n.getLastChild() == null) {
161 |       return;
162 |     }
163 | 
164 |     // Multiple if-exits can be converted in a single pass.
165 |     // Convert "if (blah) break;  if (blah2) break; other_stmt;" to
166 |     // become "if (blah); else { if (blah2); else { other_stmt; } }"
167 |     // which will get converted to "if (!blah && !blah2) { other_stmt; }".
168 |     for (Node c : n.children()) {
169 | 
170 |       // An 'if' block to process below.
171 |       if (c.isIf()) {
172 |         Node ifTree = c;
173 |         Node trueBlock, falseBlock;
174 | 
175 |         // First, the true condition block.
176 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
177 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
178 |         tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(trueBlock, falseBlock,
179 |             ifTree, exitType, labelName);
180 | 
181 |         // Now the else block.
182 |         // The if blocks may have changed, get them again.
183 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
184 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
185 |         if (falseBlock != null) {
186 |           tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(falseBlock, trueBlock,
187 |               ifTree, exitType, labelName);
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 | 
191 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
192 |         break;
193 |       }
194 |     }
195 | 
196 |     // Now try to minimize the exits of the last child, if it is removed
197 |     // look at what has become the last child.
198 |     for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getLastChild()) {
199 |       tryMinimizeExits(c, exitType, labelName);
200 |       // If the node is still the last child, we are done.
201 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
202 |         break;
203 |       }
204 |     }
205 |   }
