Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
125 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
126 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
127 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
128 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
129 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
130 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
131 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
132 | 
133 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
134 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
135 |         }
136 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
137 |       } else {
138 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
139 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 | 
143 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
144 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
145 |     }
146 |   }

===== M1011 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.identifierEscape(String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 1104-1124
Documentation:

Method code:
1104 |   static String identifierEscape(String s) {
1105 |     // First check if escaping is needed at all -- in most cases it isn't.
1106 |     if (NodeUtil.isLatin(s)) {
1107 |       return s;
1108 |     }
1109 | 
1110 |     // Now going through the string to escape non-Latin characters if needed.
1111 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
1112 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1113 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
1114 |       // Identifiers should always go to Latin1/ ASCII characters because
1115 |       // different browser's rules for valid identifier characters are
1116 |       // crazy.
1117 |       if (c > 0x1F && c < 0x7F) {
1118 |         sb.append(c);
1119 |       } else {
1120 |         appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1121 |       }
1122 |     }
1123 |     return sb.toString();
1124 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReorderConstantExpression.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReorderConstantExpression.java
Original range: 32-57
Documentation:
// to follow our naming convention.
Method code:
32 |   @Override
33 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
34 |     // if the operator is symmetric
35 |     if (NodeUtil.isSymmetricOperation(subtree)
36 |         || NodeUtil.isRelationalOperation(subtree)) {
37 |       // right value is immutable and left is not
38 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(subtree.getLastChild())
39 |           && !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(subtree.getFirstChild())) {
40 | 
41 |         // if relational, get the inverse operator.
42 |         if (NodeUtil.isRelationalOperation(subtree)){
43 |           int inverseOperator = NodeUtil.getInverseOperator(subtree.getType());
44 |           subtree.setType(inverseOperator);
45 |         }
46 | 
47 |         // swap them
48 |         Node firstNode = subtree.getFirstChild().detachFromParent();
49 |         Node lastNode = subtree.getLastChild().detachFromParent();
50 | 
51 |         subtree.addChildrenToFront(lastNode);
52 |         subtree.addChildrenToBack(firstNode);
53 |         reportCodeChange();
54 |       }
55 |     }
56 |     return subtree;
57 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getNameForObjLitKey(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 453-505
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the fully qualified name corresponding to an object literal key,
     * as long as it and its prefix property names are valid JavaScript
     * identifiers. The object literal may be nested inside of other object
     * literals.
     *
     * For example, if called with node {@code n} representing "z" in any of
     * the following expressions, the result would be "w.x.y.z":
     * <code> var w = {x: {y: {z: 0}}}; </code>
     * <code> w.x = {y: {z: 0}}; </code>
     * <code> w.x.y = {'a': 0, 'z': 0}; </code>
     *
     * @param n A child of an OBJLIT node
     * @return The global name, or null if {@code n} doesn't correspond to the
     *   key of an object literal that can be named
     */
Method code:
453 |     String getNameForObjLitKey(Node n) {
454 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
455 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isObjectLit());
456 | 
457 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
458 |       if (gramps == null) {
459 |         return null;
460 |       }
461 | 
462 |       Node greatGramps = gramps.getParent();
463 |       String name;
464 |       switch (gramps.getType()) {
465 |         case Token.NAME:
466 |           // VAR
467 |           //   NAME (gramps)
468 |           //     OBJLIT (parent)
469 |           //       STRING (n)
470 |           if (greatGramps == null || !greatGramps.isVar()) {
471 |             return null;
472 |           }
473 |           name = gramps.getString();
474 |           break;
475 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
476 |           // ASSIGN (gramps)
477 |           //   NAME|GETPROP
478 |           //   OBJLIT (parent)
479 |           //     STRING (n)
480 |           Node lvalue = gramps.getFirstChild();
481 |           name = lvalue.getQualifiedName();
482 |           break;
483 |         case Token.STRING_KEY:
484 |           // OBJLIT
485 |           //   STRING (gramps)
486 |           //     OBJLIT (parent)
487 |           //       STRING (n)
488 |           if (greatGramps != null &&
489 |               greatGramps.isObjectLit()) {
490 |             name = getNameForObjLitKey(gramps);
491 |           } else {
492 |             return null;
493 |           }
494 |           break;
495 |         default:
496 |           return null;
497 |       }
498 |       if (name != null) {
499 |         String key = n.getString();
500 |         if (TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key)) {
501 |           return name + '.' + key;
502 |         }
503 |       }
504 |       return null;
505 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.inlineNonConstants(Var,ReferenceCollection,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 254-323
Documentation:

Method code:
254 |     private void inlineNonConstants(
255 |         Var v, ReferenceCollection referenceInfo,
256 |         boolean maybeModifiedArguments) {
257 |       int refCount = referenceInfo.references.size();
258 |       Reference declaration = referenceInfo.references.get(0);
259 |       Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReference();
260 |       int firstRefAfterInit = (declaration == init) ? 2 : 3;
261 | 
262 |       if (refCount > 1 &&
263 |           isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(v, referenceInfo)) {
264 |         // if the variable is referenced more than once, we can only
265 |         // inline it if it's immutable and never defined before referenced.
266 |         Node value;
267 |         if (init != null) {
268 |           value = init.getAssignedValue();
269 |         } else {
270 |           // Create a new node for variable that is never initialized.
271 |           Node srcLocation = declaration.getNode();
272 |           value = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(srcLocation);
273 |         }
274 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
275 |         inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
276 |         staleVars.add(v);
277 |       } else if (refCount == firstRefAfterInit) {
278 |         // The variable likely only read once, try some more
279 |         // complex inlining heuristics.
280 |         Reference reference = referenceInfo.references.get(
281 |             firstRefAfterInit - 1);
282 |         if (canInline(declaration, init, reference)) {
283 |           inline(v, declaration, init, reference);
284 |           staleVars.add(v);
285 |         }
286 |       } else if (declaration != init && refCount == 2) {
287 |         if (isValidDeclaration(declaration) && isValidInitialization(init)) {
288 |           // The only reference is the initialization, remove the assignment and
289 |           // the variable declaration.
290 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
291 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
292 |           inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
293 |           staleVars.add(v);
294 |         }
295 |       }
296 | 
297 |       // If this variable was not inlined normally, check if we can
298 |       // inline an alias of it. (If the variable was inlined, then the
299 |       // reference data is out of sync. We're better off just waiting for
300 |       // the next pass.)
301 |       if (!maybeModifiedArguments &&
302 |           !staleVars.contains(v) && referenceInfo.isWellDefined() &&
303 |           referenceInfo.isAssignedOnceInLifetime()) {
304 |         List<Reference> refs = referenceInfo.references;
305 |         for (int i = 1 /* start from a read */; i < refs.size(); i++) {
306 |           Node nameNode = refs.get(i).getNode();
307 |           if (aliasCandidates.containsKey(nameNode)) {
308 |             AliasCandidate candidate = aliasCandidates.get(nameNode);
309 |             if (!staleVars.contains(candidate.alias) &&
310 |                 !isVarInlineForbidden(candidate.alias)) {
311 |               Reference aliasInit;
312 |               aliasInit = candidate.refInfo.getInitializingReference();
313 |               Node value = aliasInit.getAssignedValue();
314 |               Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
315 |               inlineWellDefinedVariable(candidate.alias,
316 |                   value,
317 |                   candidate.refInfo.references);
318 |               staleVars.add(candidate.alias);
319 |             }
320 |           }
321 |         }
322 |       }
323 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.UnionTypeBuilder.addAlternate(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/UnionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 121-214
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
121 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
122 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
123 |     // just bail out early here.
124 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
125 |       return this;
126 |     }
127 | 
128 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
129 | 
130 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
131 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
132 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
133 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
134 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
135 |     }
136 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
137 |       if (alternate.isUnionType()) {
138 |         UnionType union = alternate.toMaybeUnionType();
139 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
140 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
141 |         }
142 |       } else {
143 |         if (alternates.size() > maxUnionSize) {
144 |           return this;
145 |         }
146 | 
147 |         // Function types are special, because they have their
148 |         // own bizarre sub-lattice. See the comments on
149 |         // FunctionType#supAndInf helper and above at functionTypePosition.
150 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType() && functionTypePosition != -1) {
151 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
152 |           FunctionType other =
153 |               alternates.get(functionTypePosition).toMaybeFunctionType();
154 |           FunctionType supremum =
155 |               alternate.toMaybeFunctionType().supAndInfHelper(other, true);
156 |           alternates.set(functionTypePosition, supremum);
157 |           result = null;
158 |           return this;
159 |         }
160 | 
161 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
162 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
163 |         // one another.
164 |         int currentIndex = 0;
165 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
166 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
167 |           JSType current = it.next();
168 | 
169 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
170 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
171 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
172 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
173 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
174 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
175 |               current.isNoResolvedType() ||
176 |               alternate.hasAnyTemplate() ||
177 |               current.hasAnyTemplate()) {
178 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
179 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
180 |               return this;
181 |             }
182 |           } else {
183 |             if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
184 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
185 |               return this;
186 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
187 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
188 |               it.remove();
189 | 
190 |               if (currentIndex == functionTypePosition) {
191 |                 functionTypePosition = -1;
192 |               } else if (currentIndex < functionTypePosition) {
193 |                 functionTypePosition--;
194 |                 currentIndex--;
195 |               }
196 |             }
197 |           }
198 |           currentIndex++;
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType()) {
202 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
203 |           Preconditions.checkState(functionTypePosition == -1);
204 |           functionTypePosition = alternates.size();
205 |         }
206 | 
207 |         alternates.add(alternate);
208 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
209 |       }
210 |     } else {
211 |       result = null;
212 |     }
213 |     return this;
214 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceExitWithBreak(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java

/**
   * Replace duplicate exits in control structures.  If the node following
   * the exit node expression has the same effect as exit node, the node can
   * be replaced or removed.
   * For example:
   *   "while (a) {return f()} return f();" ==> "while (a) {break} return f();"
   *   "while (a) {throw 'ow'} throw 'ow';" ==> "while (a) {break} throw 'ow';"
   *
   * @param n An follow control exit expression (a THROW or RETURN node)
   * @return The replacement for n, or the original if no change was made.
   */
Method code:
451 |   private Node tryReplaceExitWithBreak(Node n) {
452 |     Node result = n.getFirstChild();
453 | 
454 |     // Find the enclosing control structure, if any, that a "break" would exit
455 |     // from.
456 |     Node breakTarget = n;
457 |     for (;!ControlFlowAnalysis.isBreakTarget(breakTarget, null /* no label */);
458 |         breakTarget = breakTarget.getParent()) {
459 |       if (breakTarget.isFunction() || breakTarget.isScript()) {
460 |         // No break target.
461 |         return n;
462 |       }
463 |     }
464 | 
465 |     Node follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(breakTarget);
466 | 
467 |     // Skip pass all the finally blocks because both the break and return will
468 |     // also trigger all the finally blocks. However, the order of execution is
469 |     // slightly changed. Consider:
470 |     //
471 |     // return a() -> finally { b() } -> return a()
472 |     //
473 |     // which would call a() first. However, changing the first return to a
474 |     // break will result in calling b().
475 | 
476 |     Node prefinallyFollows = follow;
477 |     follow = skipFinallyNodes(follow);
478 | 
479 |     if (prefinallyFollows != follow) {
480 |       // There were finally clauses
481 |       if (!isPure(result)) {
482 |         // Can't defer the exit
483 |         return n;
484 |       }
485 |     }
486 | 
487 |     if (follow == null && (n.isThrow() || result != null)) {
488 |       // Can't complete remove a throw here or a return with a result.
489 |       return n;
490 |     }
491 | 
492 |     // When follow is null, this mean the follow of a break target is the
493 |     // end of a function. This means a break is same as return.
494 |     if (follow == null || areMatchingExits(n, follow)) {
495 |       Node replacement = IR.breakNode();
496 |       n.getParent().replaceChild(n, replacement);
497 |       this.reportCodeChange();
498 |       return replacement;
499 |     }
500 | 
501 |     return n;
502 |   }

Method code:
212 |   private UndiGraph<Var, Void> computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(
213 |       NodeTraversal t, ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg, Set<Var> escaped) {
214 |     UndiGraph<Var, Void> interferenceGraph =
215 |         LinkedUndirectedGraph.create();
216 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
217 | 
218 |     // First create a node for each non-escaped variable.
219 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = scope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
220 |       Var v = i.next();
221 |       if (!escaped.contains(v)) {
222 | 
223 |         // TODO(user): In theory, we CAN coalesce function names just like
224 |         // any variables. Our Liveness analysis captures this just like it as
225 |         // described in the specification. However, we saw some zipped and
226 |         // and unzipped size increase after this. We are not totally sure why
227 |         // that is but, for now, we will respect the dead functions and not play
228 |         // around with it.
229 |         if (!v.getParentNode().isFunction()) {
230 |           interferenceGraph.createNode(v);
231 |         }
232 |       }
233 |     }
234 | 
235 |     // Go through each variable and try to connect them.
236 |     for (Iterator<Var> i1 = scope.getVars(); i1.hasNext();) {
237 |       Var v1 = i1.next();
238 | 
239 |       NEXT_VAR_PAIR:
240 |       for (Iterator<Var> i2 = scope.getVars(); i2.hasNext();) {
241 |         Var v2 = i2.next();
242 | 
243 |         // Skip duplicate pairs.
244 |         if (v1.index >= v2.index) {
245 |           continue;
246 |         }
247 | 
248 |         if (!interferenceGraph.hasNode(v1) ||
249 |             !interferenceGraph.hasNode(v2)) {
250 |           // Skip nodes that were not added. They are globals and escaped
251 |           // locals. Also avoid merging a variable with itself.
252 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
253 |         }
254 | 
255 |         if (v1.getParentNode().isParamList() &&
256 |             v2.getParentNode().isParamList()) {
257 |           interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
258 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
259 |         }
260 | 
261 |         // Go through every CFG node in the program and look at
262 |         // this variable pair. If they are both live at the same
263 |         // time, add an edge between them and continue to the next pair.
264 |         NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE:
265 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
266 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
267 |             continue NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE;
268 |           }
269 | 
270 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
271 |           // Check the live states and add edge when possible.
272 |           if ((state.getIn().isLive(v1) && state.getIn().isLive(v2)) ||
273 |               (state.getOut().isLive(v1) && state.getOut().isLive(v2))) {
274 |             interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
275 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
276 |           }
277 |         }
278 | 
279 |         // v1 and v2 might not have an edge between them! woohoo. there's
280 |         // one last sanity check that we have to do: we have to check
281 |         // if there's a collision *within* the cfg node.
282 |         NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE:
283 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
284 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
285 |             continue NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE;
286 |           }
287 | 
288 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
289 |           boolean v1OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v1);
290 |           boolean v2OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v2);
291 |           CombinedLiveRangeChecker checker = new CombinedLiveRangeChecker(
292 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v1, v2OutLive ? null : v2),
293 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v2, v1OutLive ? null : v1));
294 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(
295 |               compiler,
296 |               cfgNode.getValue(),
297 |               checker);
298 |           if (checker.connectIfCrossed(interferenceGraph)) {
299 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
300 |           }
301 |         }
302 |       }
303 |     }
304 |     return interferenceGraph;
305 |   }

   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node

Method code:
124 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.VAR:
127 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
128 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
129 |              child != null;) {
130 |           Node next = child.getNext();
131 |           declareVar(child);
132 |           child = next;
133 |         }
134 |         return;
135 | 
136 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
138 |           return;
139 |         }
140 | 
141 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
142 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
143 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
144 |           return;
145 |         }
146 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
147 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
148 | 
149 |       case Token.CATCH:
150 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().isName());
152 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
153 |         // is the code block
154 | 
155 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
156 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
157 | 
158 |         declareVar(var);
159 |         scanVars(block, n);
160 |         return;  // only one child to scan
161 | 
162 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
163 |         inputId = n.getInputId();
164 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);
165 |         break;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
169 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
170 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
171 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
172 |            child != null;) {
173 |         Node next = child.getNext();
174 |         scanVars(child, n);
175 |         child = next;
176 |       }
177 |     }

/**
   * Performs the line-by-line parsing of the given fileContents. This method
   * strips out JavaScript comments and then uses the abstract parseLine()
   * method to do the line parsing.
   *
   * @param filePath The path to the file being parsed. Used for reporting parse
   *     exceptions.
   * @param fileContents A reader for the contents of the file.
   */
Method code:
119 |   void doParse(String filePath, Reader fileContents) {
120 |     this.filePath = filePath;
121 |     parseSucceeded = true;
122 | 
123 |     BufferedReader lineBuffer = new BufferedReader(fileContents);
124 | 
125 |     // Parse all lines.
126 |     String line = null;
127 |     lineNum = 0;
128 |     boolean inMultilineComment = false;
129 | 
130 |     try {
131 |       while (null != (line = lineBuffer.readLine())) {
132 |         ++lineNum;
133 |         try {
134 |           String revisedLine = line;
135 |           if (inMultilineComment) {
136 |             int endOfComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/");
137 |             if (endOfComment != -1) {
138 |               revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(endOfComment + 2);
139 |               inMultilineComment = false;
140 |             } else {
141 |               revisedLine = "";
142 |             }
143 |           }
144 | 
145 |           if (!inMultilineComment) {
146 |             while (true) {
147 |               int startOfLineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("//");
148 |               int startOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("/*");
149 |               if (startOfLineComment != -1 &&
150 |                   (startOfMultilineComment == -1 ||
151 |                    startOfLineComment < startOfMultilineComment)) {
152 |                 revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(0, startOfLineComment);
153 |                 break;
154 |               } else if (startOfMultilineComment != -1) {
155 |                 int endOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/",
156 |                     startOfMultilineComment + 2);
157 |                 if (endOfMultilineComment == -1) {
158 |                   revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(
159 |                       0, startOfMultilineComment);
160 |                   inMultilineComment = true;
161 |                   break;
162 |                 } else {
163 |                   revisedLine =
164 |                       revisedLine.substring(0, startOfMultilineComment) +
165 |                       revisedLine.substring(endOfMultilineComment + 2);
166 |                 }
167 |               } else {
168 |                 break;
169 |               }
170 |             }
171 |           }
172 | 
173 |           if (!revisedLine.isEmpty()) {
174 |             // This check for shortcut mode should be redundant, but
175 |             // it's done for safety reasons.
176 |             if (!parseLine(revisedLine) && shortcutMode) {
177 |               break;
178 |             }
179 |           }
180 |         } catch (ParseException e) {
181 |           // Inform the error handler of the exception.
182 |           errorManager.report(
183 |               e.isFatal() ? CheckLevel.ERROR : CheckLevel.WARNING,
184 |               JSError.make(filePath, lineNum, 0 /* char offset */,
185 |                   e.isFatal() ? PARSE_ERROR : PARSE_WARNING,
186 |                   e.getMessage(), line));
187 |           parseSucceeded = parseSucceeded && !e.isFatal();
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 |     } catch (IOException e) {
191 |       errorManager.report(CheckLevel.ERROR,
192 |           JSError.make(filePath, 0, 0 /* char offset */,
193 |               PARSE_ERROR, "Error reading file: " + filePath));
194 |       parseSucceeded = false;
195 |     }
196 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessDefines.CollectDefines.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessDefines.java
Original range: 286-371
Documentation:

Method code:
286 |     @Override
287 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
288 |       RefInfo refInfo = allRefInfo.get(n);
289 |       if (refInfo != null) {
290 |         Ref ref = refInfo.ref;
291 |         Name name = refInfo.name;
292 |         String fullName = name.getFullName();
293 |         switch (ref.type) {
294 |           case SET_FROM_GLOBAL:
295 |           case SET_FROM_LOCAL:
296 |             Node valParent = getValueParent(ref);
297 |             Node val = valParent.getLastChild();
298 |             if (valParent.isAssign() && name.isSimpleName() &&
299 |                 name.getDeclaration() == ref) {
300 |               // For defines, it's an error if a simple name is assigned
301 |               // before it's declared
302 |               compiler.report(
303 |                   t.makeError(val, INVALID_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, fullName));
304 |             } else if (processDefineAssignment(t, fullName, val, valParent)) {
305 |               // remove the assignment so that the variable is still declared,
306 |               // but no longer assigned to a value, e.g.,
307 |               // DEF_FOO = 5; // becomes "5;"
308 | 
309 |               // We can't remove the ASSIGN/VAR when we're still visiting its
310 |               // children, so we'll have to come back later to remove it.
311 |               refInfo.name.removeRef(ref);
312 |               lvalueToRemoveLater = valParent;
313 |             }
314 |             break;
315 |           default:
316 |             if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
317 |               // Treat this as a reference to a define in the global scope.
318 |               // After this point, the define must not be reassigned,
319 |               // or it's an error.
320 |               DefineInfo info = assignableDefines.get(fullName);
321 |               if (info != null) {
322 |                 setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
323 |                 assignableDefines.remove(fullName);
324 |               }
325 |             }
326 |             break;
327 |         }
328 |       }
329 | 
330 |       if (!t.inGlobalScope() &&
331 |           n.getJSDocInfo() != null && n.getJSDocInfo().isDefine()) {
332 |         // warn about @define annotations in local scopes
333 |         compiler.report(
334 |             t.makeError(n, NON_GLOBAL_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, ""));
335 |       }
336 | 
337 |       if (lvalueToRemoveLater == n) {
338 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
339 |         if (n.isAssign()) {
340 |           Node last = n.getLastChild();
341 |           n.removeChild(last);
342 |           parent.replaceChild(n, last);
343 |         } else {
344 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.isName());
345 |           n.removeChild(n.getFirstChild());
346 |         }
347 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
348 |       }
349 | 
350 |       if (n.isCall()) {
351 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
352 |           // If there's a function call in the global scope,
353 |           // we just say it's unsafe and freeze all the defines.
354 |           //
355 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): We could be a lot smarter here. For example,
356 |           // ReplaceOverriddenVars keeps a call graph of all functions and
357 |           // which functions/variables that they reference, and tries
358 |           // to statically determine which functions are "safe" and which
359 |           // are not. But this would be overkill, especially because
360 |           // the intended use of defines is with config_files, where
361 |           // all the defines are at the top of the bundle.
362 |           for (DefineInfo info : assignableDefines.values()) {
363 |             setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
364 |           }
365 | 
366 |           assignableDefines.clear();
367 |         }
368 |       }
369 | 
370 |       updateAssignAllowedStack(n, false);
371 |     }

208 |   private Node tryFoldSimpleFunctionCall(Node n) {
209 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isCall());
210 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
211 |     if (callTarget != null && callTarget.isName() &&
212 |           callTarget.getString().equals("String")) {
213 |       // Fold String(a) to '' + (a) on immutable literals,
214 |       // which allows further optimizations
215 |       //
216 |       // We can't do this in the general case, because String(a) has
217 |       // slightly different semantics than '' + (a). See

219 |       Node value = callTarget.getNext();
220 |       if (value != null && value.getNext() == null &&
221 |           NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value)) {
222 |         Node addition = IR.add(
223 |             IR.string("").srcref(callTarget),
224 |             value.detachFromParent());
225 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, addition);
226 |         reportCodeChange();

228 |       }

===== M1157 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MaybeReachingVariableUse.computeMayUse(Node,Node,ReachingUses,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MaybeReachingVariableUse.java
Original range: 152-237
Documentation:

Method code:
152 |   private void computeMayUse(
153 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, ReachingUses output, boolean conditional) {
154 |     switch (n.getType()) {
155 | 
156 |       case Token.BLOCK:
157 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
158 |         return;
159 | 
160 |       case Token.NAME:
161 |         addToUseIfLocal(n.getString(), cfgNode, output);
162 |         return;
163 | 
164 |       case Token.WHILE:
165 |       case Token.DO:
166 |       case Token.IF:
167 |         computeMayUse(
168 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
169 |         return;
170 | 
171 |       case Token.FOR:
172 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
173 |           computeMayUse(
174 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
175 |         } else {
176 |           // for(x in y) {...}
177 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
178 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
179 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
180 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
181 |           }
182 |           if (lhs.isName() && !conditional) {
183 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(lhs.getString(), output);
184 |           }
185 |           computeMayUse(rhs, cfgNode, output, conditional);
186 |         }
187 |         return;
188 | 
189 |       case Token.AND:
190 |       case Token.OR:
191 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
192 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
193 |         return;
194 | 
195 |       case Token.HOOK:
196 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
197 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
198 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
199 |         return;
200 | 
201 |       case Token.VAR:
202 |         Node varName = n.getFirstChild();
203 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasChildren(), "AST should be normalized");
204 | 
205 |         if (varName.hasChildren()) {
206 |           computeMayUse(varName.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
207 |           if (!conditional) {
208 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(varName.getString(), output);
209 |           }
210 |         }
211 |         return;
212 | 
213 |       default:
214 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
215 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
216 |           if (!conditional) {
217 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(name.getString(), output);
218 |           }
219 | 
220 |           // In case of a += "Hello". There is a read of a.
221 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
222 |             addToUseIfLocal(name.getString(), cfgNode, output);
223 |           }
224 | 
225 |           computeMayUse(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
226 |         } else {
227 |           /*
228 |            * We want to traverse in reverse order because we want the LAST
229 |            * definition in the sub-tree....
230 |            * But we have no better way to traverse in reverse other :'(
231 |            */
232 |           for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getChildBefore(c)) {
233 |             computeMayUse(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
234 |           }
235 |         }
236 |     }
237 |   }

===== M1191 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 159-205
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
159 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
160 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
161 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
162 |       case Token.BLOCK:
163 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
164 |       case Token.TRY:
165 |         return true;
166 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
167 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
168 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
169 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
170 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
171 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
172 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
173 |         // child.
174 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
175 |       case Token.WHILE:
176 |       case Token.DO:
177 |       case Token.IF:
178 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
179 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
180 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
181 | 
182 |       case Token.FOR:
183 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
184 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
185 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
186 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
187 |         // That way the following:
188 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
189 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
190 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
191 |           // TODO(user): Investigate how we should handle the case where
192 |           // we have a very complex expression inside the FOR-IN header.
193 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
194 |         } else {
195 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
196 |         }
197 |       case Token.SWITCH:
198 |       case Token.CASE:
199 |       case Token.CATCH:
200 |       case Token.WITH:
201 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
202 |       default:
203 |         return false;
204 |     }
205 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 147-210

Method code:
147 |   @Override
148 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
149 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !n.isName() ||
150 |         parent.isFunction()) {
151 |       // Don't rename named functions.
152 |       return;
153 |     }
154 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
155 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
156 |     if (vNode == null) {
157 |       // This is not a local.
158 |       return;
159 |     }
160 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
161 | 
162 |     if (!usePseudoNames) {
163 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
164 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
165 |         return;
166 |       }
167 | 
168 |       // Rename.
169 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
170 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
171 | 
172 |       if (parent.isVar()) {
173 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
174 |       }
175 |     } else {
176 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
177 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
178 |       // make this fast.
179 |       String pseudoName = null;
180 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
181 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
182 |         Var iVar = i.next();
183 | 
184 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
185 |         // and it is merged with the current coalescedVar.
186 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
187 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
188 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
189 |         }
190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       // Keep its original name.
193 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
194 |         return;
195 |       }
196 | 
197 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
198 | 
199 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
200 |         pseudoName += "$";
201 |       }
202 | 
203 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
204 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
205 | 
206 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && parent.isVar()) {
207 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
208 |       }
209 |     }
210 |   }

/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>This enforces the Google const name convention, that the first character
   * after the last $ must be an upper-case letter and all subsequent letters
   * must be upper case. The name must be at least 2 characters long.
   *
   * <p>Examples:
   * <pre>
   *      aaa          Not constant - lower-case letters in the name
   *      A            Not constant - too short
   *      goog$A       Constant - letters after the $ are upper-case.
   *      AA17         Constant - digits can appear after the first letter
   *      goog$7A      Not constant - first character after the $ must be
   *                   upper case.
   *      $A           Constant - doesn't have to be anything in front of the $
   * </pre>
   */
Method code:
70 |   @Override
71 |   public boolean isConstant(String name) {
72 |     if (name.length() <= 1) {
73 |       return false;
74 |     }
75 | 
76 |     // In compiled code, '$' is often a namespace delimiter. To allow inlining
77 |     // of namespaced constants, we strip off any namespaces here.
78 |     int pos = name.lastIndexOf('$');
79 |     if (pos >= 0) {
80 |       name = name.substring(pos + 1);
81 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
82 |         return false;
83 |       }
84 |     }
85 | 
86 |     return isConstantKey(name);
87 |   }

===== M1238 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.canInline(Reference,Reference,Reference)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 519-583
Documentation:
/**
     * @return true if the provided reference and declaration can be safely
     *         inlined according to our criteria
     */
Method code:
519 |     private boolean canInline(
520 |         Reference declaration,
521 |         Reference initialization,
522 |         Reference reference) {
523 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(declaration)
524 |           || !isValidInitialization(initialization)
525 |           || !isValidReference(reference)) {
526 |         return false;
527 |       }
528 | 
529 |       // If the value is read more than once, skip it.
530 |       // VAR declarations and EXPR_RESULT don't need the value, but other
531 |       // ASSIGN expressions parents do.
532 |       if (declaration != initialization &&
533 |           !initialization.getGrandparent().isExprResult()) {
534 |         return false;
535 |       }
536 | 
537 |       // Be very conservative and do no cross control structures or
538 |       // scope boundaries
539 |       if (declaration.getBasicBlock() != initialization.getBasicBlock()
540 |           || declaration.getBasicBlock() != reference.getBasicBlock()) {
541 |         return false;
542 |       }
543 | 
544 |       // Do not inline into a call node. This would change
545 |       // the context in which it was being called. For example,
546 |       //   var a = b.c;
547 |       //   a();
548 |       // should not be inlined, because it calls a in the context of b
549 |       // rather than the context of the window.
550 |       //   var a = b.c;
551 |       //   f(a)
552 |       // is OK.
553 |       Node value = initialization.getAssignedValue();
554 |       Preconditions.checkState(value != null);
555 |       if (value.isGetProp()
556 |           && reference.getParent().isCall()
557 |           && reference.getParent().getFirstChild() == reference.getNode()) {
558 |         return false;
559 |       }
560 | 
561 |       if (value.isFunction()) {
562 |         Node callNode = reference.getParent();
563 |         if (reference.getParent().isCall()) {
564 |           CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
565 |           // Bug 2388531: Don't inline subclass definitions into class defining
566 |           // calls as this confused class removing logic.
567 |           SubclassRelationship relationship =
568 |               convention.getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
569 |           if (relationship != null) {
570 |             return false;
571 |           }
572 | 
573 |           // issue 668: Don't inline singleton getter methods
574 |           // calls as this confused class removing logic.
575 |           if (convention.getSingletonGetterClassName(callNode) != null) {
576 |             return false;
577 |           }
578 |         }
579 |       }
580 | 
581 |       return canMoveAggressively(value) ||
582 |           canMoveModerately(initialization, reference);
583 |     }

460 |

/**
     * Determines whether this block is guaranteed to begin executing before
     * the given block does.
     */
Method code:
703 |     boolean provablyExecutesBefore(BasicBlock thatBlock) {
704 |       // If thatBlock is a descendant of this block, and there are no hoisted
705 |       // blocks between them, then this block must start before thatBlock.
706 |       BasicBlock currentBlock;
707 |       for (currentBlock = thatBlock;
708 |            currentBlock != null && currentBlock != this;
709 |            currentBlock = currentBlock.getParent()) {
710 |         if (currentBlock.isHoisted) {
711 |           return false;
712 |         }
713 |       }
714 | 
715 |       if (currentBlock == this) {
716 |         return true;
717 |       }
718 |       if (isGlobalScopeBlock() && thatBlock.isGlobalScopeBlock()) {
719 |         return true;
720 |       }
721 |       return false;
722 |     }

===== M1348 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 76-116
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a expression. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function.
   * Note: unlike getBooleanValue this function does not return UNKNOWN
   * for expressions with side-effects.
   */
Method code:
76 |   static TernaryValue getImpureBooleanValue(Node n) {
77 |     switch (n.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
79 |       case Token.COMMA:
80 |         // For ASSIGN and COMMA the value is the value of the RHS.
81 |         return getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
82 |       case Token.NOT:
83 |         TernaryValue value = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
84 |         return value.not();
85 |       case Token.AND: {
86 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
87 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
88 |         return lhs.and(rhs);
89 |       }
90 |       case Token.OR:  {
91 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
92 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
93 |         return lhs.or(rhs);
94 |       }
95 |       case Token.HOOK:  {
96 |         TernaryValue trueValue = getImpureBooleanValue(
97 |             n.getFirstChild().getNext());
98 |         TernaryValue falseValue = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
99 |         if (trueValue.equals(falseValue)) {
100 |           return trueValue;
101 |         } else {
102 |           return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
103 |         }
104 |       }
105 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
106 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
107 |         // ignoring side-effects
108 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
109 | 
110 |       case Token.VOID:
111 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
112 | 
113 |       default:
114 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n);
115 |     }
116 |   }

/**
   * Gets all the dependencies of the given roots. The inputs must be returned
   * in a stable order. In other words, if A comes before B, and A does not
   * transitively depend on B, then A must also come before B in the returned
   * list.
   *
   * @param sorted If true, get them in topologically sorted order. If false,
   *     get them in the original order they were passed to the compiler.
   */
Method code:
210 |   public List<INPUT> getDependenciesOf(List<INPUT> roots, boolean sorted) {
211 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(inputs.containsAll(roots));
212 |     Set<INPUT> included = Sets.newHashSet();
213 |     Deque<INPUT> worklist = new ArrayDeque<INPUT>(roots);
214 |     while (!worklist.isEmpty()) {
215 |       INPUT current = worklist.pop();
216 |       if (included.add(current)) {
217 |         for (String req : current.getRequires()) {
218 |           INPUT dep = provideMap.get(req);
219 |           if (dep != null) {
220 |             worklist.add(dep);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |     }
225 | 
226 |     ImmutableList.Builder<INPUT> builder = ImmutableList.builder();
227 |     for (INPUT current : (sorted ? sortedList : inputs)) {
228 |       if (included.contains(current)) {
229 |         builder.add(current);
230 |       }
231 |     }
232 |     return builder.build();
233 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeCondition(Node)

/**
   * Try to minimize conditions expressions, as there are additional
   * assumptions that can be made when it is known that the final result
   * is a boolean.
   *
   * The following transformations are done recursively:
   *   !(x||y) --> !x&&!y
   *   !(x&&y) --> !x||!y
   *   !!x     --> x
   * Thus:
   *   !(x&&!y) --> !x||!!y --> !x||y
   *
   *   Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made
   */
Method code:
1126 |   private Node tryMinimizeCondition(Node n) {
1127 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
1128 | 
1129 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1130 |       case Token.NOT:
1131 |         Node first = n.getFirstChild();
1132 |         switch (first.getType()) {
1133 |           case Token.NOT: {
1134 |               Node newRoot = first.removeFirstChild();
1135 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1136 |               reportCodeChange();
1137 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1138 |               // NOT children are handled below.
1139 |               return newRoot;
1140 |             }
1141 |           case Token.AND:
1142 |           case Token.OR: {
1143 |               // !(!x && !y) --> x || y
1144 |               // !(!x || !y) --> x && y
1145 |               // !(!x && y) --> x || !y
1146 |               // !(!x || y) --> x && !y
1147 |               // !(x && !y) --> !x || y
1148 |               // !(x || !y) --> !x && y
1149 |               // !(x && y) --> !x || !y
1150 |               // !(x || y) --> !x && !y
1151 |               Node leftParent = first.getFirstChild();
1152 |               Node rightParent = first.getLastChild();
1153 |               Node left, right;
1154 | 
1155 |               // Check special case when such transformation cannot reduce
1156 |               // due to the added ()
1157 |               // It only occurs when both of expressions are not NOT expressions
1158 |               if (!leftParent.isNot()
1159 |                   && !rightParent.isNot()) {
1160 |                 // If an expression has higher precedence than && or ||,
1161 |                 // but lower precedence than NOT, an additional () is needed
1162 |                 // Thus we do not preceed
1163 |                 int op_precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType());
1164 |                 if ((isLowerPrecedence(leftParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1165 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(leftParent, op_precedence))
1166 |                     || (isLowerPrecedence(rightParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1167 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(rightParent, op_precedence))) {
1168 |                   return n;
1169 |                 }
1170 |               }
1171 | 
1172 |               if (leftParent.isNot()) {
1173 |                 left = leftParent.removeFirstChild();
1174 |               } else {
1175 |                 leftParent.detachFromParent();
1176 |                 left = IR.not(leftParent).srcref(leftParent);
1177 |               }
1178 |               if (rightParent.isNot()) {
1179 |                 right = rightParent.removeFirstChild();
1180 |               } else {
1181 |                 rightParent.detachFromParent();
1182 |                 right = IR.not(rightParent).srcref(rightParent);
1183 |               }
1184 | 
1185 |               int newOp = (first.isAnd()) ? Token.OR : Token.AND;
1186 |               Node newRoot = new Node(newOp, left, right);
1187 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1188 |               reportCodeChange();
1189 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1190 |               // AND and OR children below.
1191 |               return newRoot;
1192 |             }
1193 | 
1194 |            default:
1195 |              TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(first);
1196 |              if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1197 |                boolean result = nVal.not().toBoolean(true);
1198 |                int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1199 |                return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1200 |              }
1201 |         }
1202 |         // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the NOT
1203 |         // children in the general case in the main post-order traversal.
1204 |         return n;
1205 | 
1206 |       case Token.OR:
1207 |       case Token.AND: {
1208 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
1209 |         Node right = n.getLastChild();
1210 | 
1211 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1212 |         // the children, this can't be done in the general case.
1213 |         left = tryMinimizeCondition(left);
1214 |         right = tryMinimizeCondition(right);
1215 | 
1216 |         // Remove useless conditionals
1217 |         // Handle four cases:
1218 |         //   x || false --> x
1219 |         //   x || true  --> true
1220 |         //   x && true --> x
1221 |         //   x && false  --> false
1222 |         TernaryValue rightVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right);
1223 |         if (NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right) != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1224 |           int type = n.getType();
1225 |           Node replacement = null;
1226 |           boolean rval = rightVal.toBoolean(true);
1227 | 
1228 |           // (x || FALSE) => x
1229 |           // (x && TRUE) => x
1230 |           if (type == Token.OR && !rval ||
1231 |               type == Token.AND && rval) {
1232 |             replacement = left;
1233 |           } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1234 |             replacement = right;
1235 |           }
1236 | 
1237 |           if (replacement != null) {
1238 |             n.detachChildren();
1239 |             parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1240 |             reportCodeChange();
1241 |             return replacement;
1242 |           }
1243 |         }
1244 |         return n;
1245 |       }
1246 | 
1247 |       case Token.HOOK: {
1248 |         Node condition = n.getFirstChild();
1249 |         Node trueNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
1250 |         Node falseNode = n.getLastChild();
1251 | 
1252 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1253 |         // the result children, this can't be done in the general case.
1254 |         // The condition is handled in the general case in #optimizeSubtree
1255 |         trueNode = tryMinimizeCondition(trueNode);
1256 |         falseNode = tryMinimizeCondition(falseNode);
1257 | 
1258 |         // Handle four cases:
1259 |         //   x ? true : false --> x
1260 |         //   x ? false : true --> !x
1261 |         //   x ? true : y     --> x || y
1262 |         //   x ? y : false    --> x && y
1263 |         Node replacement = null;
1264 |         TernaryValue trueNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(trueNode);
1265 |         TernaryValue falseNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(falseNode);
1266 |         if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE
1267 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1268 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1269 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1270 |           replacement = condition;
1271 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE
1272 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1273 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1274 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1275 |           replacement = IR.not(condition);
1276 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1277 |           // Remove useless true case.
1278 |           n.detachChildren();
1279 |           replacement = IR.or(condition, falseNode);
1280 |         } else if (falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1281 |           // Remove useless false case
1282 |           n.detachChildren();
1283 |           replacement = IR.and(condition, trueNode);
1284 |         }
1285 | 
1286 |         if (replacement != null) {
1287 |           parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1288 |           n = replacement;
1289 |           reportCodeChange();
1290 |         }
1291 | 
1292 |         return n;
1293 |       }
1294 | 
1295 |       default:
1296 |         // while(true) --> while(1)
1297 |         TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(n);
1298 |         if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1299 |           boolean result = nVal.toBoolean(true);
1300 |           int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1301 |           return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1302 |         }
1303 |         // We can't do anything else currently.
1304 |         return n;
1305 |     }
1306 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 830-857
Documentation:
/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
830 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
831 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
832 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
833 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
834 |         if (handler.isFunction()) {
835 |           return;
836 |         }
837 |         Preconditions.checkState(handler.isTry());
838 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
839 | 
840 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
841 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
842 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
843 |           } else {
844 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
845 |           }
846 |         } else { // Has a catch.
847 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
848 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
849 |             return;
850 |           } else {
851 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
852 |           }
853 |         }
854 |         lastJump = handler;
855 |       }
856 |     }
857 |   }

Documentation:

Method code:
210 |   void addOp(String op, boolean binOp) {
211 |     maybeEndStatement();
212 | 
213 |     char first = op.charAt(0);
214 |     char prev = getLastChar();
215 | 
216 |     if ((first == '+' || first == '-') && prev == first) {
217 |       // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of
218 |       // things like "x + ++y" or "x++ + ++y"
219 |       append(" ");
220 |     } else if (Character.isLetter(first) &&
221 |                isWordChar(prev)) {
222 |       // Make sure there is a space after e.g. instanceof , typeof
223 |       append(" ");
224 |     } else if (prev == '-' && first == '>') {
225 |       // Make sure that we don't emit -->
226 |       append(" ");
227 |     }
228 | 
229 |     // Allow formatting around the operator.
230 |     appendOp(op, binOp);
231 | 
232 |     // Line breaking after an operator is always safe. Line breaking before an
233 |     // operator on the other hand is not. We only line break after a bin op
234 |     // because it looks strange.
235 |     if (binOp) {
236 |       maybeCutLine();
237 |     }
238 |   }

484 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
485 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
486 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
487 |     if (node.isBlock() && parent != null &&
488 |         parent.isTry() &&
489 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
490 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
491 |       return;
492 |     }
493 | 
494 |     // A block transfer control to its first child if it is not empty.
495 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();
496 | 
497 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that
498 |     // function (unless it is called)
499 |     while (child != null && child.isFunction()) {
500 |       child = child.getNext();
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     if (child != null) {
504 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFallThrough(child));
505 |     } else {
506 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFollowNode(node, this));
507 |     }
508 | 
509 |     // Synthetic blocks
510 |     if (parent != null) {
511 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
512 |         case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
513 |         case Token.CASE:
514 |         case Token.TRY:
515 |           break;
516 |         default:
517 |           if (node.isBlock() && node.isSyntheticBlock()) {
518 |             createEdge(node, Branch.SYN_BLOCK, computeFollowNode(node, this));
519 |           }
520 |           break;
521 |       }

639 |           return newNode(Token.EXPR_RESULT, Node.newNumber(0));

644 |       }

647 |       if (isUnnamedFunction) {
648 |         // Old Rhino tagged the empty name node with the line number of the
649 |         // declaration.

663 |       // AstNode, so there's nothing that has the actual line number that it
664 |       // appeared on.  We know the paren has to appear on the same line as the
665 |       // function name (or else a semicolon will be inserted.)  If there's no
666 |       // function name, assume the paren was on the same line as the function.
667 |       // TODO(bowdidge): Mark line number of paren correctly.
668 |       Name fnName = functionNode.getFunctionName();
669 |       if (fnName != null) {
670 |         lp.setLineno(fnName.getLineno());
671 |       } else {
672 |         lp.setLineno(functionNode.getLineno());
673 |       }
674 |       int lparenCharno = functionNode.getLp() +
675 |           functionNode.getAbsolutePosition();
676 | 
677 |       lp.setCharno(position2charno(lparenCharno));
678 |       for (AstNode param : functionNode.getParams()) {
679 |         Node paramNode = transform(param);
680 |         // When in ideMode Rhino can generate a param list with only a single
681 |         // ErrorNode. This is transformed into an EMPTY node. Drop this node in
682 |         // ideMode to keep the AST in a valid state.
683 |         if (paramNode.isName()) {
684 |           lp.addChildToBack(paramNode);

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:
2407 |   static boolean isLatin(String s) {
2408 |     char LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN = 0x7f;
2409 |     int len = s.length();
2410 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
2411 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
2412 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
2413 |         return false;
2414 |       }
2415 |     }
2416 |     return true;
2417 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

/**
   * Use "return x?1:2;" in place of "if(x)return 1;return 2;"
   */
Method code:
303 |   private Node tryReplaceIf(Node n) {
304 | 
305 |     for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
306 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()){
307 |       if (child.isIf()){
308 |         Node cond = child.getFirstChild();
309 |         Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
310 |         Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
311 |         Node nextNode = child.getNext();
312 | 
313 |         if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null
314 |             && isReturnBlock(thenBranch)
315 |             && nextNode.isIf()) {
316 |           Node nextCond = nextNode.getFirstChild();
317 |           Node nextThen = nextCond.getNext();
318 |           Node nextElse = nextThen.getNext();
319 |           if (thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextThen)) {
320 |             // Transform
321 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) return 1;
322 |             // to
323 |             //   if (x||y) return 1;
324 |             child.detachFromParent();
325 |             child.detachChildren();
326 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.OR, cond);
327 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
328 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
329 |             reportCodeChange();
330 |           } else if (nextElse != null
331 |               && thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextElse)) {
332 |             // Transform
333 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) foo() else return 1;
334 |             // to
335 |             //   if (!x&&y) foo() else return 1;
336 |             child.detachFromParent();
337 |             child.detachChildren();
338 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.AND,
339 |                 IR.not(cond).srcref(cond));
340 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
341 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
342 |             reportCodeChange();
343 |           }
344 |         } else if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null &&
345 |             isReturnBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpression(nextNode)) {
346 |           Node thenExpr = null;
347 |           // if(x)return; return 1 -> return x?void 0:1
348 |           if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
349 |             thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
350 |             thenExpr.detachFromParent();
351 |           } else {
352 |             thenExpr = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(child);
353 |           }
354 | 
355 |           Node elseExpr = nextNode.getFirstChild();
356 | 
357 |           cond.detachFromParent();
358 |           elseExpr.detachFromParent();
359 | 
360 |           Node returnNode = IR.returnNode(
361 |                                 IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
362 |                                     .srcref(child));
363 |           n.replaceChild(child, returnNode);
364 |           n.removeChild(nextNode);
365 |           reportCodeChange();
366 |         } else if (elseBranch != null && statementMustExitParent(thenBranch)) {
367 |           child.removeChild(elseBranch);
368 |           n.addChildAfter(elseBranch, child);
369 |           reportCodeChange();
370 |         }
371 |       }
372 |     }
373 |     return n;
374 |   }

1373 |     // Object() really refers to the built-in Object constructor

1377 |

/**
   * We could use addList recursively here, but sometimes we produce
   * very deeply nested operators and run out of stack space, so we
   * just unroll the recursion when possible.
   *
   * We assume nodes are left-recursive.
   */

741 |   private void unrollBinaryOperator(
742 |       Node n, int op, String opStr, Context context,
743 |       Context rhsContext, int leftPrecedence, int rightPrecedence) {

   * Tries apply our various peephole minimizations on the passed in node.

75 |   @Override
76 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
77 |   public Node optimizeSubtree(Node node) {
78 |     switch(node.getType()) {
79 |       case Token.RETURN: {
80 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
81 |         if (result != node) {

100 |       // with MinimizeExitPoints.

105 | 
106 |       case Token.IF:
107 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
108 |         return tryMinimizeIf(node);
109 | 
110 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
111 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
112 |         return node;
113 | 
114 |       case Token.HOOK:
115 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
116 |         return node;
117 | 
118 |       case Token.WHILE:
119 |       case Token.DO:
120 |         tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
121 |         return node;
122 | 
123 |       case Token.FOR:
124 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(node)) {
125 |           tryJoinForCondition(node);
126 |           tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
127 |         }
128 |         return node;
129 | 
130 |       case Token.TRUE:
131 |       case Token.FALSE:
132 |         return reduceTrueFalse(node);
133 | 
134 |       case Token.NEW:
135 |         node = tryFoldStandardConstructors(node);
136 |         if (!node.isCall()) {
137 |           return node;
138 |         }
139 |         // Fall through on purpose because tryFoldStandardConstructors() may
140 |         // convert a NEW node into a CALL node
141 |       case Token.CALL:
142 |         Node result =  tryFoldLiteralConstructor(node);
143 |         if (result == node) {
144 |           result = tryFoldSimpleFunctionCall(node);
145 |           if (result == node) {
146 |             result = tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(node);
147 |           }
148 |         }
149 |         return result;
150 | 
151 |       case Token.COMMA:
152 |         return trySplitComma(node);
153 | 
154 |       case Token.NAME:
155 |         return tryReplaceUndefined(node);
156 | 
157 |       case Token.BLOCK:
158 |         return tryReplaceIf(node);
159 | 
160 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
161 |         return tryMinimizeArrayLiteral(node);
162 | 
163 |       default:
164 |         return node; //Nothing changed
165 |     }
166 |   }

/**
   * TypeName := NameExpression | NameExpression TypeApplication
   * TypeApplication := '.<' TypeExpressionList '>'
   * TypeExpressionList := TypeExpression // a white lie
   */
Method code:
1766 |   private Node parseTypeName(JsDocToken token) {
1767 |     if (token != JsDocToken.STRING) {
1768 |       return reportGenericTypeSyntaxWarning();
1769 |     }
1770 | 
1771 |     String typeName = stream.getString();
1772 |     int lineno = stream.getLineno();
1773 |     int charno = stream.getCharno();
1774 |     while (match(JsDocToken.EOL) &&
1775 |         typeName.charAt(typeName.length() - 1) == '.') {
1776 |       skipEOLs();
1777 |       if (match(JsDocToken.STRING)) {
1778 |         next();
1779 |         typeName += stream.getString();
1780 |       }
1781 |     }
1782 | 
1783 |     Node typeNameNode = newStringNode(typeName, lineno, charno);
1784 | 
1785 |     if (match(JsDocToken.LT)) {
1786 |       next();
1787 |       skipEOLs();
1788 |       Node memberType = parseTypeExpressionList(next());
1789 |       if (memberType != null) {
1790 |         typeNameNode.addChildToFront(memberType);
1791 | 
1792 |         skipEOLs();
1793 |         if (!match(JsDocToken.GT)) {
1794 |           return reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.gt");
1795 |         }
1796 | 
1797 |         next();
1798 |       }
1799 |     }
1800 |     return typeNameNode;
1801 |   }
